picks.headline: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: No. 13 Texas Tech vs. No. 22 Arizona Football Game Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Texas Tech Athletics Texas Tech hosts Arizona in this big time Big 12 showdown. The Texas Tech Red Raiders need to focus on boosting their offense for this one. Quarterback Will Hammond has 1,561 passing yards, but he has thrown only six touchdowns and has six interceptions on the season. Explosive running back J'Koby Williams has 619 rushing yards and 5 TDs, but if you take away the Arizona State and Oregon State games, he has been inconsistent for the Red Raiders this season. Kenny Johnson , a receiver, is the main downfield target but only has one touchdown reception this season and, besides the Houston and Arizona State games, has not had a significant impact on the Texas Tech passing attack. All three as well as some other key offensive players need to step up and have big games against Arizona to win this game. The defense has to get back to focusing and dominating like they have for a lot of the season. The Red Raiders have one of the most ball-hawking secondary units in the country, sitting near the top of NCAA FBS with 13 interceptions. Defensive lineman A.J. Holmes Jr. anchors the front seven and has 6 sacks this season. However, the Red Raiders are coming off their first loss of the season, a 37-24 loss to Cincinnati where they gave up 427 yards and gave up four passing touchdowns. They will be seeking to bounce back at home to stay undefeated at home this season. Arizona, on the other hand, has a five-game winning streak and defeated Cincinnati by a final score of 34-7. Their only loss of the season was to BYU on the road. Veteran quarterback Noah Fifita leads the Arizona Wildcats, who again have a high-efficiency passing offense, with Fifiti already having 2,064 passing yards and 18 TDs through seven games. Kedrick Reescano leads the ground game with just over 300 rushing yards and five touchdowns, while wideout Isaiah Mizell is an explosive playmaker with 493 yards and 5 TDs this season, most of which have come in the Wildcats' last two games against Iowa State and West Virginia. Linebacker Taye Brown has a team-leading 27 tackles and leads the Wildcats defense. Edge rusher Chase Kennedy leads the team in pressure rate with 4 sacks, and the Texas Tech offensive line has a tough task trying to stop him from getting to the quarterback. Arizona has a scoring defense that gives up only 16.7 points per game, but they did give up 31 points against West Virginia. Arizona recently crushed Iowa State 39-3 and has put up a total of just over 200 points in their last five games. The Wildcats are also 2-1 on the road this season heading into Lubbock for this top 25 game. The key matchup for this game will be Noah Fifita vs. the Texas Tech secondary. Fifita’s efficient throwing (almost 74% completion rate) will face immediate tests from a Red Raider defense that excels at creating takeaways via interceptions. Another major matchup in this game pits the Red Raiders offensive line against Arizona’s front seven on defense. Texas Tech’s running offense behind J’Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner will face a challenge against an Arizona front seven that is holding opponents under 110 rushing yards per game. This game also has Big 12 Championship ramifications since both teams are deadlocked at 3-1 in conference play behind undefeated Utah, and the winner is squarely in the race for a Big 12 Championship Game berth. An early game prediction for this game that may change slightly as the injury reports for both teams come out later this week, but the Red Raiders bounce back and win a very close game by a final score of Texas Tech 28, Arizona 27. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction: Big 12 Elimination Game? Pete Fiutak Tue, October 27, 2026 at 11:28 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas Tech was cruising right along, looking like the star of the Big 12 again after a 53-25 blowout over Arizona State, and then it walked into a wall at Cincinnati, losing with a 37-24 thud. Arizona has been fantastic ever since its 28-17 loss at BYU early in the season, including a 34-7 win over Cincinnati. But it still has a few nasty games to go in November. Both teams are 6-1. The winner will be set up nicely for a College Football Playoff spot if it doesn't win the Big 12 title. The loser will still be alive for the CFP if it wins out, but getting to the Big 12 Championship in a loaded conference season will be tough. Arizona vs Texas Tech: Quick Hits Texas Tech still has to go to Oklahoma State, but it doesn't have to face BYU or Utah, and the other three games against West Virginia, at Baylor, and TCU aren't bad. Arizona gets three of its final four games at home, getting TCU and Utah next before going to Kansas State and finishing up against Arizona State. Texas Tech won the most recent matchup 28-22 in 2024 and is 5-2-1 in the series going back to 1975. How To Watch Arizona vs Texas Tech Arizona at Texas Tech Date: Saturday, October 31, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Galaxy Stadium, Lubbock, TX – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Arizona Will Win For the second time all year, Texas Tech played someone who could run well, and Cincinnati went off in the 13-point win. Houston can run. It ran 37 times for 175 yards against the Red Raiders, and lost when it couldn't hit a late two-point conversion. Cincinnati wasn't exactly more physical, but it found space on the way to a 255-yard day with big run after big run. Arizona's running game isn't a killer, but it's more than effective enough, working hand-in-hand with super-accurate quarterback Noah Fifita and an offense that's great at keeping the chains moving. Why Texas Tech Will Win Arizona doesn't take the ball away enough, and that matters in a huge way here. The Wildcats forced two takeaways in the win over Washington State, and two more in the win over West Virginia. That's about it, coming up with six on the year. Texas Tech has a huge problem with turnovers, with three against Cincinnati, two against Houston, and ten in the last five games. Don't turn it over, or at least stay even in the mistake battle, and the Red Raiders should be fine. Texas Tech has a great balance to its attack, and it needs to mix it up. BYU and West Virginia – in very different ways – both showed it's possible to move the ball efficiently against the Wildcat defense. Arizona vs Texas Tech Prediction, Betting Lines Is Arizona ready to show that it's really and truly a player, or will Texas Tech wipe away the Cincinnati loss like it was just a blip? It'll be a little of both, as Arizona controls the clock and tempo for the first half, but Texas Tech gets the pass rush working early in the second half. It'll be rough for the Red Raiders without pressuring Fifita, and they won't do enough of it over the final ten minutes. But now comes the Wildcats’ toughest test since Week 2, a trip to Lubbock to take on No. 13 Texas Tech. The Red Raiders (6-1, 3-1 Big 12) are coming off a 37-24 loss at Cincinnati, whom the UA beat 34-7 at home on Oct. 3. How will the Wildcats do in this West Texas showdown? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Texas Tech wins 28-27 Arizona has one of the top offenses in the country, landing in the top 50 in a number of categories: 2 nd in completion percentage (.738), 3 rd in third down conversion percentage (.547), 28 th in first downs, 42 nd in red zone offense (.889), 21 st in scoring offense (36.1), 12 th in team passing efficiency (169.66), and 17 th in total offense (459.4). When looking through the offensive stats, a comp for this game starts to come into focus. Houston keeps popping up in a similar position for most categories. The stats are not identical, and each team has a few strengths that the other lacks, but overall, they are fairly comparable offenses. That is relevant this week because the Cougars are the only ranked team that this week’s opponent has faced. Texas Tech took on No. 18 Houston the third week of the season. Like Saturday’s contest, it was played in Lubbock. The Red Raiders squeaked out a 28-26 win. They won their next three games handily against lesser competition before the surprising blowout upset by Cincinnati last week. It all suggests that TTU can be pushed, and perhaps even be beaten, in its home stadium. Arizona has the offense to compete. It showed last week that it can utterly shut down a team that averages just under 26 points per game. The Wildcats won’t hold TTU to three points, but they are good enough to keep this one up for grabs until the end. Ezra Amacher — Arizona wins 27- 24 Arizona is walking into a hornet’s nest in Lubbock after Texas Tech got embarrassed Cincinnati. One of the major storylines in college football this week is whether Texas Tech billionaire booster Cody Campbell is going force any personnel issues if the Red Raiders’ struggles persist. Everyone in a 100-mile radius of Lubbock knows that there is a lot more on the line Saturday than your typical Big 12 game. Another Texas Tech loss would knock the Red Raiders out of playoff contention. All that setup is to say that Arizona is facing a team that will be playing with its pants on fire. Even so, I think Noah Fifita does enough for the Wildcats to pull off one of the program’s biggest wins of the last decade. Texas Tech on paper has one of the top defenses in the Big 12, but the unit hasn’t totally lived up to the billing. Texas Tech gives up 266 passing yards per game, which is third-worst in the conference. Arizona’s passing offense is one of the best in the country, and with the Wildcats getting more receivers reps each game, I feel confident that they can successfully throw the ball Saturday. Arizona’s biggest obstacle to winning will be converting scoring opportunities on offense and limited the Red Raiders offense when they get down the field. Texas Tech’s opponents have scored on 83% of red zone drives, which is also third-worst in the Big 12. By contrast, Arizona’s red zone defense is first in the Big 12, allowing points on 67% of drives. I expect the red zone advantage to favor Arizona, allowing the Wildcats to leave Lubbock with a close win. Adam Green — Texas Tech wins 34 -24 I’d feel better had Tech not lost to Cincinnati last week. On paper Texas Tech has a better (or at least more expensive) roster. This game is in Lubbock, and it is also on Halloween. Aside from what happens on the field, there is plenty surrounding this matchup that just gives the vibe of there potentially being too much to overcome for Arizona. That said, the small spread and general vibe around each program lends itself to the idea that Arizona could leave that game Saturday with a victory and a clear path to the Big 12 title game. If Arizona can win the turnover battle and limit big plays from Tech there is then reason to believe that Noah Fifita and the Wildcats offense can move the ball. Not settling for field goal attempts will be important, of course. So yeah, Arizona could win this game. The Cats are playing excellent football and are no doubt confident they can win a big matchup on the road. But in my mind the home team will come out focused and fired up following its first loss and the environment will be such that the visitors cannot afford a slow start or to make mistakes. Asking any team to play a perfect game to have a chance to win is both unfair and unrealistic, which is why I just can’t predict an upset in this one. Juan Serrano — Texas Tech wins 31-27 It isn’t unrealistic to think that Arizona can win in Lubbock, this is a team playing with a high level of confidence and execution of its game plan. Led by Noah Fifita , the offense is moving the ball with ease and scoring almost whenever it wants to. While it is still lacking explosiveness, the run game is coming on slowly. However, this is a Red Raiders defense that is very opportunistic and athletic. It forces its opponents into mistakes that aren’t usually made. If Arizona can keep it clean on offense it will have a chance to win the game. The defense plays a lot better inside Casino Del Sol Stadium and it showed last week. Now on the road at Lubbock, it will face a challenge similar to what it saw in Provo. If the Wildcats are going to be in a position to win they will need force turnovers. Arizona only had two interceptions and five fumbles on the season, that number will need to rise on Saturday. If this game was being played in Tucson I’d probably be rolling with the Wildcats. It’s not a long road trip to Lubbock but it will end up feeling like a long trip. Texas Tech will rebound from the loss to Cincinnati with a win over Arizona. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 31-21 I’m going to go against my pre-season prediction and my better judgement here. This is 100% a game Arizona can win, and I think they do on Saturday. Texas Tech’s defense is legit. Ben Roberts and Austin Romaine are phenomenal linebackers, combining for 102 tackles, 10 TFL, 2 sacks and 3 interceptions on the year. John Curry and Brice Pollock are fantastic cover corners. AJ Holmes is a monster on the interior defensive line and leads the conference with 5.5 sacks on the year. So why would I pick Arizona? It’s because the Red Raider offense leaves a lot to be desired. Quarterback Will Hammond has not been great this season. He is completing 68% of his passes and only has 6 touchdown passes to go along with 6 picks. Hammond can make plays with his legs but I don’t foresee Arizona’s defense having an issue there. They do have some good running backs with J’koby Williams , Quinten Joyner and Cameron Dickey . Williams is sitting at a measly 7.2 yards per carry on the season and has 619 yards on the ground and 5 touchdowns to his name. Coy Eakin and Kenny Johnson are Tech’s top two receivers, with Johnson sitting just under 500 yards and a touchdown. With all that, I believe the Arizona defense can stymy the Red Raider offense. The key will be how Noah Fifita and Seth Doege plan and execute around Tech’s solid defense. Last week showed that this defense can be taken advantage of and can be scored on. If Noah plays a clean game, I don’t see how Tech can win against the Wildcat defense. Brian Pedersen — Texas Tech wins 24-20 Arizona has a 5-game win streak in consecutive seasons for the first time since 1992-93, but the difference between this year’s run and the one in 2025 is when it has happened. Last fall the Wildcats shook off back-to-back heartbreaking losses to BYU and Houston to catch fire and win out the rest of the regular season, while this time around the solid play has been happening pretty much from the outset. But Texas Tech is far better than any of the teams the UA faced during the win streak, even the Cincinnati team that beat the Red Raiders. Tech has won 12 in a row in Lubbock, where offensive coordinator Seth Doege will be returning to his old stomping grounds. And the opponent has a very high-priced roster, one that to this point hasn’t lived up to expectations. This is a game that Arizona can’t afford to fall behind by two scores in, which means keeping mistakes to a minimum. Assuming Noah Fifita has his patented solid performance, this will come down to who capitalizes on their chances the most. picks.blurb: Arizona vs. Texas Tech Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 9 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Arizona Wildcats and Texas Tech Red Raiders meet on Saturday in Lubbock in a Top 25 showdown that could have major implications on the Big 12 Championship race. Both teams enter Week 9 at 6-1 overall and 3-1 in Big 12 play, but they're coming off completely different Saturdays. Arizona made another statement by crushing Iowa State 39-3, while Texas Tech suffered its first loss of the season in a 37-24 road defeat at Cincinnati. Now, Texas Tech returns home to a place where it has won 12 straight games, while Arizona gets another opportunity to prove it belongs among the top contenders in the Big 12. The matchup also features an intriguing battle between Noah Fifita and an aggressive Texas Tech defense that leads the country with five pick-sixes this season. Here is everything you need to know about Arizona vs. Texas Tech in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Saturday's Big 12 showdown. Texas Tech vs. Arizona Odds Spread: Texas Tech -3.5 Over/Under: 54.5 Moneyline: Arizona +134/Texas Tech -160 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: Arizona's Passing Game vs. Texas Tech's Defense? The Red Raiders' defense has been underwhelming, at best. Texas Tech ranks 14th in the Big 12 Conference in passing yards allowed per game, ranking only ahead of Cincinnati and West Virginia. Now, this secondary does have 13 takeaways, which is tops in the Big 12. But that also tells me that they may be too aggressive , at times. And now they have to slow down Noah Fifita, who doesn't make many mistakes. He's thrown 18 touchdowns to just four interceptions this season and has the deepest wide receiver corps in the entire Big 12. Whoever wins this match up will win the game. Houston vs. Utah Prediction and Pick Prediction: Arizona 31, Texas Tech 24 Texas Tech was exposed last week at Cincinnati. Yes, they have talent, but they haven't been able to put it all together this season. And after Saturday, there's no evidence that it's magically going to happen against one of the most underrated teams in the country, Arizona, who is playing some of the best football in America right now. Since losing to BYU on the road (a game they led in the second half), Arizona has won five-straight games by an average of nearly 24 points. I haven't even talked about the other side of the ball, where Arizona is Top 5 in passing defense in yards allowed per game, and ranked 3rd in the Big 12 in yards allowed per carry (3.1). The front seven has been outstanding, as that impressive run defense has done it against the Top 2 rushing offenses in the league (West Virginia, Cincinnati). They've racked up 24 sacks in seven games, good for second in the Big 12, and now take on a Texas Tech offensive line that has been spotty, at best, throughout the season. Also, in a game that could come down to the final drive or two, Arizona's red zone defense ranks tops in the Big 12, while Texas Tech comes in at No. 14. And as the game wears on, the Tech defense could get worn down. Tech is second-to-last in the Big 12 in Time of Possession, while Arizona is in the Top 5, this despite having a pass-heavy offense. The icing on the cake on my pick? Special teams. Arizona is the best punt returning team in the Big 12. Texas Tech ranks 13th. These little things in a tough Top 25 match up can be the difference. And they will be come Saturday in Lubbock. And if you want to know where the sharp money is: 62% of the tickets are on Texas Tech, but over 80% of the money is on Arizona. The line opened up at Arizona +4.5 and is down to +3.5. If you can still get more than a field goal, jump on it. Arizona wins. Arizona covers. picks.headline: Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona football game, makes a score prediction
picks.blurb: Texas Tech expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm October 30, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football College football has one of the longest offseasons of any sport, which lends itself to certain players and teams generating a lot of hype and attention. Texas Tech falls squarely in that category, as its seemingly unlimited resources thanks to billionaire booster Cody Campbell made it a go-to place for top transfers out of the portal. But that also led to the ill-fated acquisition of quarterback Brendan Sorsby , who after leaving Cincinnati for Tech was revealed to have bet on college sports. Sorsby was banned by the NCAA, later reinstated, but the backlash led to him leaving the program before ever playing a game. Despite that, Tech was unbeaten before losing last week, dropping to No. 13 in the AP poll and into a tie for second place in the Big 12 with, among other teams, Arizona. That in effect makes Saturday’s matchup an unofficial elimination game for the conference title race. To better understand the Red Raiders, we reached out to Seth Jungman of Staking the Plains for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his eloquent answers to our inarticulate questions: AZ Desert Swarm: Outside of the irony of the first loss coming to Cincinnati, what were the biggest contributors to Texas Tech falling from the ranks of the unbeatens? Seth Jungman: “It’s the thing that I think Texas Tech fans have known, but maybe the national media wasn’t paying attention. I think most fans have known that the offense simply wasn’t very good and the defense isn’t as good as it was last year. Will Hammond is fine, but there’s a reason why the staff went out to get Brendan Sorsby before the season. They knew he probably wasn’t ready, but things happened and here we are. Also, I think it’s incredibly evident that the players who were part of this defense last year were truly special, particularly Jacob Rodriguez, David Bailey, and Romello Height. Getting to the quarterback to wreck offenses was the cheat code last year and this year, that’s simply not happening.” It’s fair to say that Will Hammond was not the first choice to lead this offense. How do you think he has performed to this point? What are his best attributes and where does he lack most? “I thought last week against Arizona State he took a step forward, but against Cincinnati he took two steps back. His best attributes is that he is a natural leader and he wants the ball in his hands and he wants to be the guy. My biggest problem with him is that I think he makes bad game management decisions. Knowing that the team needs points, he’ll heave the ball towards the end zone with a low chance of completion rather than take the play that keeps the drive alive. His lack of understanding of knowing when to take chances and when to churn yards is what bothers me the most.” What is the likelihood that Cameron Dickey will be back for this game? How would that impact the run game and the way J’Koby Williams, who has run for 680 yards and five touchdowns, get used? “I think chances are very good that he returns. It’s been about four weeks from the dreaded high-ankle sprain and that’s about the time. I don’t think it was a bad sprain so this game would seem about right and he was out doing some drills this past week. What Dickey offers is a guy that’s going to bruise and batter the opposing defense while Williams will break a 40-yard run in what looks like a lost play. Quinten Joyner has tried to fill that roll for Dickey, but it’s not the same. Joyner is coming off of ACL surgery and he doesn’t have the same burst he had at USC. I think the staff will likely get back to that Dickey-Williams rotation as soon as possible.” Texas Tech is second in FBS in passes intercepted (13) but has also given up 16 TD passes and is ranked third-worst in the Big 12 in pass defense. How do you expect the defense to try and stop Noah Fifita? “As mentioned above, the Texas Tech defense last year was getting to the quarterback so quickly that teams simply could not function offensively. This year . . . not so much. Fifita has rounded out to be such a good quarterback, I truly expect him to have a very good day. There’s almost no difference between his home and road stats, three picks on the road and just one at home, and he’s throwing for nearly 300 yards every time he steps on the field. That’s the kind of consistency that you expect from a senior and with Fifita’s ability to run to keep the defense honest, I expect him to do what he’s done all year long.” Who are the top defensive players that Arizona has to be most concerned with? “Defensive tackle AJ Holmes is an absolute unit and there aren’t a ton of defensive tackles that truly rush the passer, but he’s one of them. The linebacking corps is incredibly solid with Ben Roberts, John Curry and Austin Romaine. I’ll also add in Brice Pollock at cornerback. The pass defense is struggling a bit, but he’s a solid cornerback that can make plays.” Considering all the money that was spent on this team, and all the national attention it has brought on itself—thanks, Cody Campbell!—does it feel like the season is on the line in this game? How do you expect Tech to respond to that last performance? “As you have already recognized, this team is a quarterback short of maybe what it could have been. I try not to involve myself in the offseason drama. The whole thing was a mess and handled poorly. I think we’ve all moved on, but I know it still lingers and I think that Sorsby would have made a significant difference in the offense. For what Joey McGuire preaches, yes, the season is on the brink because the goal is to win the Big 12 and make the playoffs. I don’t know that a Big 12 team with two losses makes the playoff and I also don’t think that a 2-loss Big 12 team makes the championship. “I do expect Texas Tech to play much better than what they did against Cincinnati and I think it will be a much more competitive game. I also realize that Arizona’s defense is no joke and the Texas Tech offense has really only played well against defenses that aren’t very good. The offense and defense for the Red Raiders have a lot to prove against Arizona.” Prediction time. Does Arizona end the Red Raiders’ 12-game home win streak and continue its push toward the Big 12 title game or does Texas Tech get back on track? Give us a score pick. “My gut tells me that this will be an incredibly close game and Vegas thinks so as well. With a touchdown advantage, the line now sits at Texas Tech -3.5. I tend to agree, that despite the flaws that were on display against Cincinnati, I think Texas Tech does win the game, but I’d take Arizona and those points. Something like 37-34 is what I see the final score being.” Next 3 weeks could decide Big 12 football title game participants Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. Even forget the fact that the Badgers have lost four straight in this series. When Wisconsin plays Iowa, it's a battle between two like-minded programs. Two teams that want nothing more than to impose their will on opponents via a punishing ground game and stout, tenacious defense. This is the game, year in and year out, that provides the litmus test for the Badgers. Just how physical, how tough are they? How badly do they want it? picks.headline: Leistikow's Iowa-Wisconsin prediction boils down to football basics
picks.blurb: NFL MLB NBA NHL NCAA Football NCAA Basketball UFC/MMA PGA Tour Games IOWA FOOTBALL Leistikow's Iowa-Wisconsin prediction boils down to football basics Chad Leistikow Des Moines Register Updated Oct. 29, 2026, 12:09 p.m. ET Here is Chad Leistikow's pick and score prediction for Iowa vs. Wisconsin. The team that rushes for more yards has won the last 14 matchups in this series. Winning the turnover battle is a key focus for Iowa, as they have a 78-5 record under Phil Parker when doing so. IOWA CITY — Recent history favors Iowa football as it prepares for an Oct. 31 Homecoming matchup with Heartland Trophy rival Wisconsin. After going 2-8 against the Badgers from 2010 through 2021, the Hawkeyes have stolen all the momentum in this series with four consecutive wins by a (staggering) combined margin of 118-26. That includes a 79-10 advantage in the two years of Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz vs. Wisconsin’s Luke Fickell. Ferentz’s message this week before Monday’s practice, as relayed by captain Deshaun Lee, was that history doesn’t mean a thing. And that message had multiple layers, considering Iowa is coming off a deflating 13-10 loss at Minnesota while Wisconsin is coming into Kinnick Stadium after an inspiring 24-7 win over USC. “Nothing's guaranteed in this game. Nothing that you did last year. It's week-to-week,” said Lee, a fifth-year senior cornerback who has become a catalyst on this defense with three interceptions. “We're focused on just preparing well to put ourselves in a good position.” To deliver its best product against the Badgers, Iowa can’t think about how it dominated this matchup a year ago or how poorly it played last week. However, we can learn from Iowa’s recent dominance over Wisconsin and what might unlock a win. And here are the two biggest keys to the Hawkeye victory. No. 1: Win the rushing battle In the 28-year Ferentz era, the team that has the most rushing yards is 23-2 in this series, including in each of the last 14 meetings. Almost hilariously, Iowa rushed 45 times for 52 yards (while Wisconsin totaled 51 rushing yards) in a rugged 24-10 Hawkeyes win in 2022. Rushing for more yards than Wisconsin will be hard to do in this one, because that’s the Badgers’ main offensive game … while Iowa has failed to reach 100 rushing yards in four of its five games against power-conference opponents. But … in the three meetings under Wisconsin defensive coordinator Mike Tressel (starting in 2023), the Badgers have allowed Iowa a stunning 739 rushing yards on 138 attempts. That equates to 5.4 yards per carry and 246.3 yards per game. This Wisconsin defense is allowing only 2.8 per carry and 96.4 per game, but that’s the mission for Iowa’s offensive line in this one. And good news, it looks like the Hawkeyes will have running back L.J. Phillips available after he wasn't included on the initial injury report . This might be a game to unleash the South Dakota transfer who led all of FCS in rushing last season. “Hear the call in the huddle, get up to the line, have a plan,” Iowa offensive tackle Jack Dotzler said, “and then just all just roll together.” No. 2: Win the turnover battle Iowa is 78-5 under defensive coordinator Phil Parker when winning the turnover margin. Yet Iowa’s minus-1 margin for the season is a troubling sign, but one that Ferentz is absolutely stressing more than usual this week. “We've operated that way for 20-plus years,” Ferentz said. “… It gets down to players appreciating and understanding the value of ball security, and then secondly keeping their concentration where it needs to be. That's where the experience and inexperience can play in a little bit.” During Iowa’s four-game win streak vs. the Badgers, the turnover margins by game are: plus-2, plus-2, plus-2 and plus-2. And Iowa scored on defense in 2022 (Cooper DeJean pick-six) and 2023 (safety). The key for Iowa is to stop the run and force Wisconsin quarterback Colton Joseph to make careless or daring throws. He’s been intercepted five times, but all five picks have come in games in which he has attempted 30 or more passes. He’s been turnover-free in three straight contests while limiting his attempts (20, 16 and 14). Chad Leistikow's Iowa vs. Wisconsin football game prediction Wisconsin (5-2, 3-1 Big Ten) at No. 24 Iowa (5-2, 2-2) Time, TV, line: Oct. 31 at 11 a.m. CT, FOX, Iowa by 3½ points Where Wisconsin has the edge: The Badgers have been aggressive and productive defensively and can unleash outside linebacker Sebastian Cheeks, who leads the Big Ten in pass pressures with 34. Wisconsin is allowing just 11.3 points per game in Big Ten play, the best conference mark for any Power 4 team. Abu Sama III, an Iowa State transfer, has big-play ability as part of a potent Badgers backfield. Wisconsin kicker Gavin Lahm is 10-for-12 on field goals and hasn't missed inside 46 yards, with a long of 51. Where Iowa has the edge: The Hawkeyes have better pass-catching talent, led by receivers Tony Diaz and Reece Vander Zee and tight end DJ Vonnahme. Iowa defensive tackle Bryce Hawthorne is playing at a high level and can help disrupt Wisconsin's run-game plan. The Hawkeyes haven't leaned into Kinnick Stadium in a tense game since Week 2 against Iowa State, and the home crowd should be a benefit ... especially with San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle revving it up as the honorary captain. Prediction: Iowa 17, Wisconsin 9 ... In a reverse of the 2016 score between these teams at Kinnick Stadium, Iowa's defense delivers another dominant day. Zach Lutmer makes his first major impact in a game this season, and Diaz finds the end zone for the first time since Week 1. picks.blurb: The Associated Press ranked the Badgers No. 25, their first appearance in the rankings since 2023. However, you are only as good as your last win. For Luke Fickell’s squad, its next opportunity for that win comes this week against the US LBM Coaches Poll's No. 24 team, the Iowa Hawkeyes . So far this season, the Hawkeyes (5-2) have lost to Ohio State and Minnesota. Both of those losses came in their last three games. ESPN's Bill Connelly’s SP+ metric is one of the most well-respected in the sport; it often provides a great compass for that week’s games. Connelly recently revealed his prediction for when the Badgers travel to Kinnick Stadium. He projects the Hawkeyes to win 23-17, giving a 65% chance that Iowa takes down Fickell’s squad. What would a loss mean for the Badgers? Overall, dropping to 5-3 still provides a strong foundation for the final four games. In those, Wisconsin would likely be favored by varying amounts, creating opportunities to capitalize on the momentum it has built. Without a doubt, this is UW's toughest remaining road game on the schedule even though three of Wisconsin's final five games are away from home. away.blurb: The Badgers' final injury report ahead of the primetime showdown certainly helps them out ahead of what's just about as close to a must-win game as you can get. The Trojans roll into Madison with a stacked team. Their offense, in particular, is loaded with young , dynamic skill position talent and their quarterback is none other than the decorated Jayden Maiava, whose 2,045 passing yards were second in the country ahead of Week 8. Thus, Wisconsin needs its secondary to have its best game yet this season. The return of Robinson is monumental; he's been lockdown in the Badgers' back end this fall. USC's defensive line, meanwhile, has been a problem as well. The Trojans' run defense ranks a very respectable No. 33 nationally allowing 111.0 yards per game, and there's a handful of playmakers up front the Badgers must account for, namely true freshman defensive end Luke Wafle, who's racked up 27 tackles, two sacks, 16 pressures and one pass-breakup. Thus, the return of Kawecki is a big deal as well. Final Score predictions for Ole Miss Rebels and Auburn Tigers Scott Wachter-Imagn Images and John Reed-Imagn Images Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 29, 2026 at 6:54 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Ole Miss Rebels are in a position to bounce back against an Auburn team that looked bad last week. The Ole Miss Rebels lost to the Texas Longhorns last week. The loss does not help their College Football Playoff chances at all. In fact, they now have a 44% chance of making the postseason. A win over the Auburn Tigers on Saturday would move that to 53%, according to A to Z's Simulator. As for Auburn, they have a 1% chance to make it . And, with a win over Ole Miss, that jumps to just 7%. They then have to play Alabama in Week 13, too. This could be a great game with real implications. So, our experts broke it all down. Final Score Predictions for Ole Miss vs. Auburn Ole Miss 34, Auburn 16: Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame Ole Miss takes care of business against Auburn with a 34-16 win, thanks largely to a monster performance from quarterback Trinidad Chambliss. With Kewan Lacy sidelined, the Rebels needed someone to step up offensively, and Chambliss delivered. He makes plays with both his arm and his legs, keeping Auburn's defense on its heels and helping Ole Miss avoid a major drop-off without one of its key offensive weapons. The Rebels find success through the air and do enough on the ground to keep the offense balanced, putting Auburn in a difficult spot for most of the afternoon. Auburn's offensive struggles continue as the Tigers struggle to put together consistent drives against an Ole Miss defense that takes advantage of their mistakes. The Tigers may find a few scoring chances, but they lack the consistency to make this a competitive second half. As Auburn's offense stalls, Chambliss and the Rebels capitalize, gradually building a comfortable lead and putting the game out of reach. Ole Miss leaves with a 34-16 win, and Chambliss proves he can carry a significant portion of the offensive load even without Lacy in the lineup. Ole Miss 35, Auburn 20: Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama After a big win over Georgia a couple of weeks ago, the Tigers came back to Earth against LSU last weekend, and things won't get any easier against Ole Miss this week. The Rebels will look to bounce back after a loss to the Longhorns, with their playoff lives on the line. I don't know how Auburn plans to contain Trinidad Chambliss, but he'll be back and hungry to make plays after a down performance against Texas. An Auburn defense that has struggled for much of the season may be the perfect scenario for this team and Trinidad Chambliss. Give me Ole Miss by a wide margin. Ole Miss 38, Auburn 24: Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida I was high on Auburn after their upset win over Georgia and genuinely thought they'd beat the LSU Tigers. Well, they instead got smoked and got exposed as not ready to compete. Ole Miss is now on life support in the playoff race, having lost to Florida and Texas, two other SEC foes who also have two losses. Trinidad Chambliss was very inconsistent against the Longhorns and will use this as a get-right game for the stretch run. Ole Miss 31, Auburn 23: Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee In a game the Rebels cannot afford to lose to stay in the playoff picture, it starts with a bit of a scare. Byrum Brown and the Tigers get off to another strong road start, building an early lead and leaning on the ground game to shorten the game and keep Trinidad Chambliss on the sideline longer than Rebel fans want. But the Rebels get things going quickly in the second half. As Sam Leavitt and the Tigers did from the jump last week against Auburn, Chambliss and his targets get in rhythm and push ahead in the third quarter. Auburn keeps it interesting until the end, but they can't pull off the big road upset for the second time in as many tries. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gives key injury update on Tai Buster
away.blurb: Sophomore Tai Buster was expected to be a key piece of Auburn's offensive line rotation this season, but a preseason setback has kept him away from the field . This week, Auburn head coach Alex Golesh gave a positive report for Buster's availability, saying he could be available to play as early as a few weeks. “Tai (Buster) has worked his tail off. I give Tai a lot of credit. He is working through return to play," Golesh said Monday. "The hope is that here in a couple of weeks, we get him fully integrated in practice, and it gives us a chance to see where he is." For injured players, it can take days or weeks to catch up and return to their routine, but Golesh says that will not be the case for Buster. Buster has remained immersed in practice and should return to full speed quickly. "He’s been engaged; I give him a lot of credit again, he’s been engaged," Golesh said. "He’s itching to get back out there. I thought when he got banged up, he was competing at a high level. We’re excited to get him back here soon.” Adding Buster to the rotation will not solve every issue the offensive line faces, but having an extra body will help keep linemen, especially at guard, fresh during Auburn's final stretch of regular-season games. The Tigers will be without Buster for their next game, Saturday at Ole Miss, but he could return in November to assist Auburn with their pursuit of bowl eligibility. home.blurb: THURSDAY Ole Miss vs. Auburn Injury Report: Crawford, Davis Still Questionable; Lacy Out ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – The first SEC availability report of Auburn week is out, and No. 12 Ole Miss has two key starters listed as questionable for Saturday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and left tackle Terez Davis are both questionable on the initial report, released at 7:10 p.m. CT on Wednesday. Running back Kewan Lacy is out, as expected, after dislocating his shoulder in last week's loss at Texas. Jalyn Crawford questionable after big night at Texas Pete Golding said Monday that Crawford “played his best game” at Texas and is “starting to show who we thought he was.” Losing him would be a big blow to a secondary that is already thin. Safety Edwin Joseph is out again as he works his way back from a procedure, and Golding said Monday he did not “feel great” about Joseph's chances this week. Safety MJ Preston, cornerback Cedrick Beavers, cornerback Iverson McCoy and safety Nascar McCoy are also out. Terez Davis questionable, but trending up Davis missed the Texas game after being a game-time decision, and he is questionable again to start the week. But Golding sounded confident Monday that his left tackle will be back. “Probably could have done it, but we didn't know what it was going to look like after and could have made it worse,” Golding said of holding Davis out in Austin. “So that's one definitely that we feel like, throughout this week, that we'll get back for this weekend.” Without Davis, Connor Howes moved to left tackle and Tommy Kinsler started at right tackle, and the line did not allow a sack. Howes and center Brycen Sanders are both listed as probable. Kewan Lacy out, Makhi Frazier steps in Ole Miss will also be without wide receivers Izaiah Hartrup and Kervin Johnson Jr., linebacker Ant Davis Jr. and offensive lineman Emanuel Faulkner. home.headline: Top Auburn WR Listed as Questionable Ahead of Ole Miss Matchup
home.blurb: Top Auburn WR Listed as Questionable Ahead of Ole Miss Matchup Skip to main content SI.COM Koger was listed as questionable on the Tigers’ initial injury report Thursday meaning that he has around a 50% chance to play, while offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring are listed as out. At this time, it is unclear as to why exactly Koger is listed as questionable, but it goes without saying that losing his production would be a significant blow for the Tigers, as he currently ranks third among all Tigers in total receiving yards. Koger was a four-star recruit out of St. Frances Academy in Baltimore, Maryland, when he signed with Alex Golesh and the USF Bulls, earning playing time quite early in his young career. Last season, his freshman year, Koger hauled in 38 Byrum Brown passes for 597 yards and eight touchdowns before transferring to the Plains this past offseason. If Koger is ruled out for the game against Ole Miss, the Tigers still have plenty of other talent to turn to in the interim, including fellow USF transfer receiver Christian Neptune, who completed a touchdown pass to Singleton against Georgia, as well as DeShawn Spencer, a true freshman who has hauled in 10 passes for 90 yards and two touchdowns so far this season. The Auburn Tigers are looking to rebound from a devastating loss to LSU, in which the Bayou Bengals came to town and routed the home team by 21 points, though that effort may get a little more difficult with the potential absence of one key wide receiver: Jeremiah Koger. The Maryland native was highly anticipated on the Plains and has lived up to a large part of those expectations, though he has not yet quite turned in the statistical production of the Tigers’ top two receivers, Keshaun Singleton and Chas Nimrod, both of whom are also new Auburn transfers from USF. So far this season, Koger has caught 14 passes for 230 yards, both stats ranking third on the team. Notably, however, Koger has yet to bring in a touchdown for the Tigers this year, which is quite surprising given his production at USF last season. Singleton and Nimrod have worked to make up for that, though, hauling in a combined five touchdown passes from Brown this season. They’ve also combined for 69 total receptions and 771 receiving yards, a high mark for any Auburn duo. The Tigers are scheduled to square off against Ole Miss this Saturday, October 31, at 11:45 a.m. CT, in a matchup that is scheduled to be broadcast on SEC Network. The Bulldogs and Gators are playing a one-off game in Atlanta this season , and one next year in Tampa as Jacksonville (the traditional home for this game) rebuilds its stadium. The anticipation for the game is growing as the weekend grows near. What’s also growing is the betting line for the game. On Sunday FanDuel listed the Bulldogs as a 9.5-point favorite over the Gators. DraftKings had UGA as a 10.5-point favorite in the contest. Both betting houses now have Georgia as a 12.5-point favorite to win the game. The move in the line is a fairly significant one - placing the game firmly into double-digit territory. Of course, betting lines are only an indication of what experts feel is expected to happen - they are not a guarantee of an outcome. There are two reasons the line has be crept up over the week. First, both of Florida’s quarterbacks are injured in some form. Athens-area native Aaron Philo started the first six games of the Gators’ season, but missed Florida’s 27-24 win at Texas with a shoulder injury. Tramell Jones started for the Gators in that game and guided the Gators to an upset in Austin. Jones has “wear-and-tear” injuries. Georgia football TE Jaden Reddell celebrates with Georgia football RB Chauncey Bowens after scoring a touchdown against Vanderbilt. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he would not name a starter at that time. “Both guys are available - believe in both guys,” Sumrall told reporters. “Not going to name a starter today. We need both those guys to be ready to play.” Both Gator quarterbacks were listed as questionable Wednesday night on the SEC’s mandated injury report. In addition, Georgia got very good news with an upgrade for running back Chauncey Bowens, who was upgraded to questionable from out, which is where he’s been the last few weeks. Bowens scored the game-winning touchdown against the Gators last year in Jacksonville. Second, there was likely some overreaction to Georgia’s upset loss to Auburn at home, and the Gators’ upset win on the road at Florida. Most of the summer this game was listed around the 12-point mark. Florida’s play early in the season dropped the number under ten points, but that recovered to back over double digits after Florida was blown out in back-to-back losses to Missouri and South Carolina. But only twice in modern history has a double-digit favorite lost this game (1997 and 2014). In both upsets turnovers and a robust run game powered the underdog to an unexpected win. Since 2010, the Bulldogs have been favored to beat the Gators 13 times in the last 16 games. Georgia is 11-5 straight up against the Gators since then - losing in overtime as a one-point favorite in 2010, a 10-point favorite in 2014, a 3-point underdog in 2015, a 6.5-point underdog in 2016 and a 3-point favorite in 2020. On average the Dawgs have been a 6.5-point favorite to beat Florida since 2010. The team that runs the ball better in the World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party is 15-1 since 2010 (2020 - Florida, 44-28). Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. This time the Bulldogs are listed as a 10.5-point favorite to topple the Gators in Atlanta on Halloween according to Draft Kings . It is another in a string of games where the Bulldogs have been favorites to beat their biggest SEC rival. Georgia has not been an underdog against the Gators since 2016 - the first year Kirby Smart took over as the head coach in Athens. Should the line remain unchanged at kickoff it would be the sixth time since that year that Georgia has been a double-digit favorite to win the game. Georgia’s 24-20 win over Gators in Jacksonville last fall was the first time UGA had been favored by fewer than ten points in five seasons. One of the keys to success for Kirby Smart’s program over his tenure in Athens has been the Dawgs’ ability to slow or even stop the Gators running the ball effectively. Georgia football RB Nate Frazier (3) pushes off Florida Gators defensive back Cormani McClain. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Florida has not eclipsed the 120-yard mark on the ground since going for 161 in a 34-7 loss to the Dawg in 2021. Florida has not eclipsed the 120-yard mark on the ground since going for 161 in a 34-7 loss to the Dawg in 2021. Florida has been up and down running the ball this season - even with one of the best running backs in the nation… Jadan Baugh. Baugh has been solid against the Dawgs - going for 136 yards on 32 carries with a touchdown. With the Gators’ quarterback situation in flux, Baugh might be the singularly-important player in the game. South Carolina and Missouri slowed the Atlanta native in their two wins against the Gators. But against Texas, Baugh was a workhorse again - scoring once on the ground after carrying the ball 25 times for 91 yards. Baugh blistered Auburn (162 yards; 3 TDs) and Ole Miss (142 yards; 3 TDs) earlier this season. Georgia is 7-4 all time when allowing a 100-yard rusher under Kirby Smart. Georgia had a tremendous start to the season defending the run, but has had back-to-back games on run defense that are as bad as they have had dating back to the end of the 2024 season. The Bulldogs have only covered once in the last four games against the Gators - in 2023 thanks to a late-game touchdown from Dwight Phillips. This is the first time since 2018 that UGA is coming off a loss going into a scheduled bye week. The Dawgs are 17-3 all time after losses and 12-3 after a bye under Kirby Smart. The Dawgs and Gators meet in Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta for the first time ever. The game, which is traditionally held in Jacksonville, is on a two-year hiatus from there so that massive renovations can take place to upgrade the facility there. Georgia has played in Mercedes-Benz Stadium each year it has been open. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Who will win Florida vs Georgia: Georgia -11.5 Kirby Smart has owned the Florida vs. Georgia rivalry recently, winning eight of the last nine games. But without knowing which version of Florida we'll get, I would only take the Bulldogs up to -12.5 . Georgia's defense is far more trustworthy than Florida's, ranking 14th nationally in available yards percentage (35.7%) , 21st in defensive success rate (35.4%), and holding six of seven opponents to 20 or fewer points. With athletes like Chris Cole and Ellis Robinson IV, Georgia is well-equipped to deal with Buster Faulkner's misdirection-heavy offense. Plus, the Gators' top two QBs ( Aaron Philo , Tramell Jones Jr. ) are questionable , and while I expect them to play, it could impact their consistency. In a high-scoring game, Georgia's defense will make enough stops to cover. TOP PICK Florida vs Georgia Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 Georgia has been an Over machine this season, hitting it in six of seven games, despite its defense allowing just 15.9 points per game. I like the Over to hit at 55.5 or better for the fifth time in the last seven Cocktail Parties, especially given Faulkner's familiarity with Smart and Georgia's defense. Faulkner worked for Smart at Georgia for three years before spending the last three seasons as Georgia Tech's offensive coordinator; his offenses averaged 24.6 points and 392 yards against the Bulldogs. With one of the top running backs in the country in Jadan Baugh , who ranks top 10 in forced missed tackles (40), Florida should score 20+. Its defense will do the rest of the job for the Over. Florida has one of the worst defenses in the Power Four, r anking 125th in the country in defensive success rate (49.5%) , and it hasn't played an offense as efficient as Georgia's yet this season. Florida vs Georgia combo Some weeks Florida looks like a College Football Playoff team (against Ole Miss and Texas ), and other weeks it looks like it might not win eight games (against Missouri and South Carolina ). Which version will come to play in the World's Largest Cocktail Party? If Auburn hadn't improbably upset the Bulldogs the last time they played, they would probably be closer to 14.5-point favorites because of Florida's defensive struggles and offensive injuries. Coming out of a bye, I expect Smart to have Georgia ready to roll in a rivalry game he's dominated and to pull away in the second half against a Florida defense that ranks second-worst in havoc rate in the SEC (14.5%). Collin Wilson Wed, October 28, 2026 at 5:14 PM UTC · 13 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Week 9 of the college football season is already upon us. We have a number of intriguing matchups this week, and it all starts on Friday night. To kick off my Week 9 betting card, I'm looking toward a Big 12 battle between the Baylor Bears — who just fired their head coach — and the UCF Knights, who just pulled off their first-ever upset over a top-five team. On Saturday, we'll begin in Iowa City, where the Iowa Hawkeyes will look to bounce back in a trophy game against the No. 25 Wisconsin Badgers. Then, in the SEC, the No. 17 Florida Gators meet the No. 3 Georgia Bulldogs for the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party in Atlanta. Finally, to close it all out, we'll take a look at a Big Ten tilt between the No. 2 Ohio State Buckeyes and USC Trojans. With so much to get to, let's dive into my college football picks and NCAAF predictions for the Week 9 games on Saturday, October 31. Be sure to download the Action Network app for more expert picks and analysis! College Football Picks, Predictions The team logos in the table below represent each of the matchups that Action Network senior writer Collin Wilson is targeting from Week 9's slate of games. Baylor has fired head coach Dave Aranda, a move made after a critical loss to Kansas in Week 8. The former LSU defensive coordinator leaves Waco with a 40-40 overall mark, not good enough for the current administration. Former athletic director Mack Rhoades took a separation agreement in November 2025, leaving Aranda's future in doubt under new athletic director Doug McNamee. Defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman, recently brought in from Kansas State , will serve as the interim coach as Baylor looks to reach bowl season. The Baylor defense was never the issue this season, allowing an average of 16.1 points per game. The offense, under transfer quarterback DJ Lagway, has severely struggled with coordinator Jake Spavital. The Bears sit outside the top 110 in Success Rate on offense, relying on pass explosives as the only means of creating scoring opportunities. Despite the struggles as a whole, Lagway has seen improvement from his days at Florida with an increase in big-time throws and a lower turnover-worthy play rate. The Bears struggle in scoring position, averaging just 3.3 points on 50 offensive possessions inside the opponent's 40-yard line. Red-zone efficiency has been a constant failure all season, ranking 121st in touchdown percentage. Only half of the 30 possessions that made it into the red zone have resulted in a Baylor touchdown. UCF had one of the more advantageous spots of the entire college football calendar when hosting BYU , as the Cougars were coming off a program-defining win over Notre Dame . The overtime game provided all the thrills for a college football masterpiece, as the Knights took a field-storming victory with an 89% post-game win expectancy. Backup quarterback Keyone Jenkins led UCF to four methodical drives and an explosive passing attack, tossing six explosives through the air. The defense had the assignment of slowing down Heisman hopeful Bear Bachmeier , and it limited the BYU quarterback to just 37 rushing yards on 15 carries. The biggest factor was basic fundamentals, as the Knights missed just nine tackles in the game to add on a PFF tackling grade that ranks in the top 25. The Cougars' high-octane offense was limited to just a single rush explosive. It makes sense considering UCF's defense ranks 15th in Line Yards and top-40 in Rush EPA allowed. The handicap on this game forces handicappers to look beyond the advanced statistics, as the Baylor program is in flux. Klanderman isn't expected to win the job as Baylor's head coach, as McNamee has made it clear a coach with Texas roots and an offensive mindset will be the next hire. The downstream effect of the coaching search could create outside noise for coordinators and players looking for their next stop if they don't make a bowl game. Statistically, Baylor could have a hard time generating points against the UCF defense. The Bears have generated plenty of available yards to create scoring opportunities, but a rank outside the top 100 in Finishing Drives will go against a Knights defense that's 32nd in limiting opponents in scoring position. With the expectation that UCF will have a hangover from one of the most electric college football games of the season, a first-half under is the look from a statistical and spot perspective. There are also advantages for UCF in the run game against the Baylor defense. The Bears have a top-10 unit in terms of Rushing Success Rate allowed but have a mid-FBS average of 50% against teams that use inside zone. The Knights run a heavy amount of inside zone through Jenkins and running back Duke Watson . A boost could be in store if quarterback Alonza Barnett III returns from a hamstring injury. The James Madison transfer suited up for the BYU game but did not play for the fifth straight game. Any contribution from Barnett would further solidify UCF's position. Pick: 1H Under 24.5 · UCF ML (-110 or Better) Florida entered the bye week on a high note, beating a top-10 team on the road for the first time since 2012. The Gators remain at two losses on the season in the thick of the SEC race and a potential spot in the College Football Playoff, but a date with Georgia in the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party comes first. The biggest takeaway from the victory over Texas came from backup quarterback Tramell Jones Jr. tossing a couple of touchdowns in a mistake-free game. The sophomore completed 22-of-35 passes while chipping in 50 rushing yards with an even split of scrambles and designed run calls. On the other side, the defense continues to rank as one of the best in the nation when creating chaos. The top-10 Havoc numbers are led by 53 tackles for loss , nine forced fumbles and 34 passes defensed. Five players on the defensive line have generated double-digit pressures, while seven different defenders have multiple pass breakups. The issue with Florida's defense is its performance close to the goal line, ranking 95th in red-zone defense. The Gators have allowed 40 opponent possessions to cross the 40-yard line and are giving up an average of 4.4 points per trip . Georgia's first loss to Auburn in nine years comes as a result of ball protection. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was responsible for two interceptions and a fumble, an uncharacteristic set of events for the senior. Up until the Alabama game in Week 6, Stockton managed to throw just six interceptions and lose three fumbles since the beginning of the 2025 season. In the past two games, the Georgia quarterback has committed two fumbles and three interceptions . There's the case that Stockton had too much of the load against Auburn, taking a critical hit in the first series of the game. Running back Chauncey Bowens has missed multiple games with injury, while Nate Frazier was ineffective coming off a rib injury, finishing with less than 20 rushing yards. The bye week should provide the best health for the offense in weeks, as head coach Kirby Smart described Bowens as day-to-day . Stockton should also be fully recovered from any shoulder or concussion symptoms. The Bulldogs defense continues to be one of the best nationally in defending the run, ranking top-25 in Rushing Success Rate allowed and Defensive Line Yards. Georgia grades out as one of the best tackling teams nationally, as no individual player has missed more than five tackles this season . Cornerback Ellis Robinson IV has been one of the best at shutting down wideouts all season with five pass breakups and an interception. Florida has three primary run concepts in the arsenal: outside zone, counter and power. The most successful and explosive of the group comes from power attempts with a heavy box, led by running back Jadan Baugh. The junior has 100 more rushing attempts than any other player on the team, running an even split of zone read and non-zone read concepts. Despite the highly successful numbers against zone read and counter, Georgia has been horrific against power concepts this season . The Bulldogs have elite numbers in Defensive Finishing Drives and red-zone prevention, ranking fifth in red-zone drives allowed. away.headline: Florida football injury update | Two QBs listed as questionable for Georgia
away.blurb: News Sports Things To Do Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals FOOTBALL Florida football injury update | Two QBs listed as questionable for Georgia Kevin Brockway Gainesville Sun Updated Oct. 28, 2026, 8:56 p.m. ET Florida football made its quarterback situation even more cloudy heading into its matchup against rival Georgia in Atlanta. The top two Florida Gators quarterbacks on the depth chart − Aaron Philio and Tramell Jones Jr.−are both listed as questionable for UF's showdown with the Bulldogs. Philo, who started UF's first six games for the Gators , sat out Florida 's game against Texas on October 17 with a shoulder injury. Jones, who led UF to an upset win over the Longhorns by passing for 155 yards and 2 TDs, is dealing with an undisclosed injury. "He’s got a couple of bumps and bruises, too, now," Sumrall said. "And he had, you know, pulled the guy fresh out of that garage and he goes and plays, and he got a couple fender-benders. So, there's some bumps and bruises he's dealing with that are new. I noticed it last week." Also on the availability report, inside linebacker Jaden Robinson and wide receiver Bailey Stockton are listed as doubtful for UF, while running back Duke Clark has been upgraded to questionable. Wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed UF's last three games with a knee strain, is listed as probable. For Georgia, wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, outside linebacker Amaris Williams and safety Tyriq Green have been ruled out. Preseason All-SEC safety KJ Bolden is listed as questionable, along with running back Chauncey Bowens and wide receiver Isiah Canon. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said both practiced this week and hinted Jones was dealing with issues following the Texas win during his opening week press conference on October 26. If Jones and Philo both can't go, Florida would turn to its third-string quarterback, redshirt junior Aidan Warner, or true freshman Will Griffin. Warner appeared in the Florida-Georgia game in 2024 when DJ Lagway went down with a hamstring injury and made one career start the following week at Texas. No. 20 Florida (5-2. 3-2 SEC) is looking to break five-game losing streak against the Bulldogs (6-1, 4-1 SEC) when the two schools meet on Saturday, October 31 (3:30 p.m., ABC). The game, traditionally held in Jacksonville, was moved to Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta due to the $1.4 billion renovation at EverBank Stadium for the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars. picks.blurb: Previewing Northwestern's Upcoming Matchup Against Oregon as They Prepare to Face Another Tough Test on the Road Skip to main content SI.COM Olympic Sports More from Northwestern Wildcats On SI FOOTBALL The Wildcats hit the road once again, this time traveling west to Eugene, Oregon, for a Big Ten showdown against the Oregon Ducks on Saturday at 2:30 p.m. CT. Oregon enters Saturday’s matchup looking to bounce back following a 21-10 loss to Illinois. The Ducks have been without starting quarterback Dante Moore for the past three games, and recent reports indicate he is unlikely to return this season after suffering a concussion earlier this year against USC. Oregon now sits at 10th in the conference with a 4-3 overall record this season. Meanwhile, the Wildcats enter Saturday’s matchup fresh off a commanding 42-14 home victory over Rutgers, a win that propelled Northwestern to No. 20 in the AP Poll. A familiar face will return to Eugene this weekend, as former Oregon head coach Chip Kelly will take on the Ducks, this time as the Wildcats’ offensive coordinator. Under Kelly’s leadership, Northwestern’s offense has emerged as one of the best in the Big Ten this season, ranking third in the conference in total yards and points per game and second in rushing yards per game. The Wildcats head to Eugene looking to build on their success on both sides of the ball and extend their four-game winning streak. A major contributor to Northwestern’s offensive success this season has been quarterback Aidan Chiles, this week’s Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week, who has thrown for over 1,600 yards and 12 touchdowns, while recording just one interception. Chiles was dominant last time out against Rutgers, throwing for 219 yards and passing for three touchdowns, while rushing for 83 yards and two touchdowns. Alongside Chiles, wide receiver Griffin Wilde has been another standout for David Braun’s squad, recording 39 receptions for 615 yards and four touchdowns this season. Northwestern’s rushing attack has also been a major part of its offensive success, led by the dynamic running back duo of Caleb Komolafe and Joseph Himon II, who have combined for over 900 rushing yards this season. Komolafe delivered an especially impressive performance against Rutgers, rushing for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats’ convincing victory. Defensively, Northwestern has remained stout this season, spearheaded by defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and line backer Braydon Brus. Despite missing the last two games due to injury, Fitzgerald has recorded 49 tackles and two interceptions this season. The defensive back leads the Big Ten in tackles per game with nine, followed closely by Brus in second with 8.9. Brus leads the defensive unit with 62 tackles and has also notched an interception and fumble recovery this season. Despite Dante Moore’s potential absence the rest of the season, Northwestern will still face a tough challenge on the road against a talented Oregon team. Quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas have shared playing time the past three games for the Ducks. Raiola struggled in last weekend’s loss to Illinois, completing 27 of 41 passes for 246 yards, as the defeat dealt a major blow to Oregon’s hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff for a third consecutive season. Mehringer had been promoted to the role at the start of the season after Will Stein departed to become the head coach at Kentucky, but his tenure was ultimately short-lived. This weekend’s matchup will be just the third time that both teams will be meeting, and the first time that they will match up at Autzen Stadium. They have split results, with Oregon taking the most recent matchup last season. Stay up to date on the Wildcats by bookmarking Northwestern On SI and follow us on Twitter. After entering the season ranked as high as they've ever been, the Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) are unranked and out of the immediate College Football Playoff race after a stunning loss to Illinois on the road . The Ducks don't have much time to lick their wounds, either. After firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer and announcing quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the 2026 season , one-loss Northwestern comes to town . Chip Kelly, who guided Oregon to a national championship game appearance as head coach over a decade ago, is the Wildcats' offensive coordinator. "It's almost like you're playing three different offenses," Oregon coach Dan Lanning said of Northwestern. "The new wrinkles that (Kelly) has at Northwestern, some of the old flavor that he has that he's carried all the way to his time back here at Oregon. There's always going to be something new when you walk into a game that it's going to be like he's never put this on film. He might not know how you're going to line up against it, and you have to figure it out there within the rules of your defense and how you execute." How it happened Oregon football, Dan Lanning react to lifeless loss vs. Illinois Oregon moves forward without its star QB and offensive coordinator Oregon vs. Northwestern scouting report Why Oregon has an advantage: The Ducks will have the home crowd behind them in Eugene and also have deep familiarity with Northwestern's starting quarterback, Aidan Chiles. The senior signal-caller started his career at Oregon State before transferring to Michigan State in 2024. Chiles played at Autzen Stadium in that year and had a rough outing, completely just 10 of 17 passes for 154 yards in a 31-10 loss. The Ducks found ways to rattle Chiles early, and with a strong pass rush in recent weeks they could do so again Saturday. Why Northwestern has an advantage: The Wildcats, under first-year offensive coordinator and former Ducks coach Chip Kelly, have one of the most efficient offenses in the country and don't make many mistakes. Northwestern isn't necessarily an offensive juggernaut, but it ranks fifth in the country in turnover margin and moves the ball methodically while keeping opposing teams out of the end zone defensively. Though the Wildcats' defense gives up plenty of yards, they rank in the top 25 in scoring defense allowing just 16.6 points per game. Oregon running back Jordon Davison, right, eludes Illinois defensive lineman Carter Janki and scores a touchdown during the first half at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, Illinois on Oct. 24, 2026. Oregon vs. Northwestern injury updates Note: Official availability reports, mandated by the Big Ten, are released every day starting at 5 p.m. Wednesday leading up to kickoff. This story was published before the reports were made public. For Oregon: The Ducks will have a good chunk of playmakers returning to the sideline this weekend after sitting out last week due to unknown reasons. Evan Stewart, who was out last week after a DUII arrest, is expected back, as are Jalen Lott and Messiah Hampton. Lanning did not elaborate why Hampton and Lott missed last week. The coach also announced quarterback Dante Moore will likely miss the rest of the 2026 season after sustaining a concussion in late September. For Northwestern: The Wildcats were without several key contributors last week in a win against Rutgers, especially defensively. Second-leading tackler Robert Fitzgerald was held out, as well as defensive lineman Brendan Flakes. Oregon defensive back Peyton Woodyard, left, tries to catch the ball as it is deflected off Illinois wide receiver Collin Dixon during the second half at Gies Memorial Stadium in Champaign, Illinois on Oct. 24, 2026. Oregon vs. Northwestern: 4 bold predictions Ducks will mostly contain vaunted Northwestern run game Though Chiles has been successful through the air in recent weeks, Northwestern's bread and butter is establishing the ground game. After a subpar performance stopping the run last week against Illinois, Oregon's defense will show up ready to play and stifle backs Caleb Komolafe, Joseph Himon II and Gavin Sawchuk. Outside of games versus Oklahoma State and Illinois, Oregon's run defense has been sound and it'll look like a motivated group against a physical Wildcats team this weekend. Gage Hurych will have a bounce-back performance vs. Wildcats After missing three field goals last week in a loss to Illinois, all from 40 yards or more, junior kicker Gage Hurych will have a strong game against Northwestern. The Wildcats give up a lot of yards with a bend-but-don't-break defense but are elite in the red zone, an area where Oregon's offense struggles. Northwestern opponents only score a touchdown on 40% of possessions that reach the red zone. If Oregon's offense stalls as it gets closer to the end zone, look for Hurych to have a bounce-back performance with more manageable field-goal attempts. Ducks' defense will keep them in it until the end Though Oregon's offense will likely still have trouble after firing Drew Mehringer, its defense will respond and keep them in the game until the fourth quarter. Outside of a couple of broken off runs in a loss to Illinois, the Ducks' defense has been one of the top units in the country over the last month and that will continue against Northwestern this weekend. It just won't be enough to get a win, unless the offense really corrects itself. Here is how the A to Z Sports team sees Saturday’s game playing out. A to Z Sports Score Predictions Tyler Forness — A to Z Sports Florida Prediction: Northwestern 24, Oregon 14 Going into the season, projecting the Wildcats to beat the Ducks would have been a shocker. On Halloween, it won’t be a trick, but rather a Wildcat treat. What Chip Kelly has done with this offense and head coach David Braun overall has been very impressive. They aren’t just 6-1 overall this season, but rank seventh in adjusted EPA/play on offense. It’s been a wild turnaround, and even though the Ducks have a huge talent surplus, their coaching staff is not in a great place, and Dante Moore is out for the year. The Northwestern playoff push continues on after a big win Saturday. Rob Gregson — A to Z Sports Alabama Prediction: Northwestern 25, Oregon 20 The 2026 Oregon Ducks are a case study in why turnover at the coordinator positions is problematic. That, and why if you can go to the NFL and be a high first-rounder, you should. The loss of Dante Moore for the season underscores what has been a messy situation from start to finish on offense this season. Will Stein has the Wildcats thriving in Kentucky, and that loss is felt in a major way. But the defense hasn’t been much better. Now, a Northwestern squad that is willing to run the ball at will is heading to Oregon, and I think they will challenge the physicality of the Ducks in a major way. Oregon doesn’t have the firepower to score, and it will be a massive win for Northwestern. Craig Smith — A to Z Sports Miami Prediction: Northwestern 23, Oregon 19 Boy, how the perception of this game has changed since Labor Day weekend. Oregon’s playoff goose is cooked at 4-3 after losses to Oklahoma State, UCLA, and Illinois. Dante Moore is done for the season. Offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer was fired after the loss to the Illini. In other words, things are a mess, particularly on the offensive side of the ball. This one stays close at Autzen Stadium, as the Ducks move the ball relatively well early on. But Northwestern, while allowing 364.6 yards per game, has been very good at keeping the point total lower, ranking 22nd nationally at 16.6 points per game. The Wildcats force some early field goals, and their ground game, paced by Caleb Komolafe, takes over the second half as the Wildcats get out of town at 7-1 and firmly in the Big Ten and playoff races. Northwestern is a good team, and their story is amazing. But I think Oregon’s overall talent and coaching advantage in this one is just too good. Northwestern does have a +9 turnover margin. They force them, and they don’t commit them. Oregon cannot say the same. They have also scored on 96% of their red zone opportunities this year, which is extremely good. So, I can see why that would be enticing. But this Oregon roster is just too talented to give up on yet. Still, the talent on this roster is difficult to overlook, particularly in a game that could come down to one or two critical possessions. Northwestern’s ability to run the football and protect the ball makes the Wildcats a dangerous opponent, especially against an Oregon team that has struggled to find consistency. However, I expect the Ducks to make just enough plays offensively to survive a tight finish. Northwestern has a legitimate opportunity to pull off the upset, but I’m giving Oregon the narrow edge at Autzen Stadium. Consensus: Can Northwestern Finish the Upset? The common theme is Oregon’s offensive instability following Dante Moore’s season-ending injury and the coaching changes that have contributed to an uneven campaign. Northwestern’s ability to run the football, limit opponents’ scoring, and capitalize on mistakes gives the Wildcats a path to a major road victory. Justin Churchill and I are the exceptions, backing Oregon to lean on its roster talent and home-field advantage. Both expect a close game, and I am predicting a one-point Ducks victory. Regardless of the final score, Northwestern has an opportunity to turn an impressive start into a season-defining result. Oregon, meanwhile, needs to show that its talent can overcome the problems that have derailed its season. If the Wildcats establish the run and force Oregon into uncomfortable passing situations, an upset in Eugene could be very much in play.
