RELATED : Experts release new Oregon-Northwestern predictions, picks and best bets after Dante Moore officially ruled out for season For four weeks since Moore was struck in the head while sliding to end a run during a 41-27 win at USC, the team watched him return to practice and hoped he would play again. The offense scored just 42 points over the three games he missed. “It was very heartbreaking to hear, but at the same time, we’ve kind of been getting used to other quarterbacks playing,” he said. “So, in terms of football plays and stuff like that, we just got to rock out with what we’ve been doing. So, we’re already used to it, but I feel for him deeply.” This week, the Ducks also fired offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. His biggest failing was not generating enough offense with a marginal and unsettled offensive line. Dante Moore was also out. Plus, in two games, the Ducks were missing the team’s top two wide receivers, Jeremiah McClellan and Evan Stewart. At Illinois, the Ducks were missing four of their top five wide receivers. Coach Dan Lanning announced on Monday that Moore would miss the remainder of the season . Moore missed three games after entering concussion protocol following a vicious hit to the head on Sept. 26 at USC. The news, relayed to the team on Sunday, left several players devastated as Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) prepares to host No. 20 Northwestern (6-1, 3-1) on Saturday. “It was bad news to hear,” Oregon senior tight end Jamari Johnson said. “That was my guy.” Saturday’s 21-10 loss at Illinois pretty much ended the Ducks’ realistic hope of reaching the College Football Playoff. The next day, Moore told the team he wouldn’t be returning to the field. “Of course, that’s something that’s very heartbreaking, being that he was the first guy to even speak to me when I first got here,” sophomore wide receiver Dakorien Moore said. “We got the same last name, to give us even more connection. So, just that bond that we have in general, I feel for him.” Dante Moore led the Ducks to the national semifinals last season, where they lost to Indiana. Soon after, Moore returned to Oregon to develop and chase a national title — a decision Johnson recalled with both fondness and sadness. “That was like one of the first flashbacks I had in my mind when he said (he was done for the season),” Johnson said. “So, it’s my dog, man. home.blurb: David Banks-Imagn Images David Banks-Imagn Images Northwestern Football: Key Injury Updates Ahead of Oregon Alex Kwiatkowski Partner Oct 30, 2026 12:52 AM Published Oct 30, 2026 12:52 AM Northwestern’s latest injury report has Luke Dehnicke off the list, Robert Fitzgerald out and several Wildcats sidelined ahead of Saturday’s matchup against Oregon. With Northwestern preparing to face an Oregon team that will be looking to adjust offensively, having another experienced receiving option available could be important. Dehnicke’s removal from the availability report is an encouraging sign, although his availability should be confirmed closer to kickoff. Fitzgerald, meanwhile, remains out. The safety has been an important part of Northwestern’s defense, and his absence presents another challenge for a unit preparing to face the Ducks on the road. Northwestern’s defense will need to communicate effectively and limit explosive plays as Oregon adjusts to a new offensive play-caller . Brendan Flakes is listed as doubtful, while Robby Preckel remains questionable. Flakes has contributed on special teams, including blocking a key field goal in Northwestern’s win over Michigan State . His potential absence could affect the Wildcats’ special teams depth against Oregon. Several other players remain out, including offensive lineman Ezomo Oratokhai, Josh Fussell, Daniel Anderson, Max Mohring, Jason Reynolds II, Callen Campbell, Qayvier Johnson, Jacob Miller and Chris Petrucci. Braxton Strong is also listed as out after previously being listed as doubtful. With several players still sidelined, Northwestern will need contributions from across its roster. Dehnicke’s potential return would provide a welcome boost, while the defense must find ways to compensate for Fitzgerald’s absence as the Wildcats look to extend their winning streak. The Sooners have won a game followed by a loss three times this season and sit at 4-3 after defeating Mississippi State on the road this past weekend. Wide receiver Nyck Harbor is a big-play threat at any moment. Defensively, Dylan Stewart wreaks havoc on most offenses he faces — he's recorded two sacks and forced three fumbles in four games this season. The case for South Carolina: Beamer has the Gamecocks rolling. Momentum can be a real thing. The Sooners will likely need kicker Tate Sandell to be better, though. (Sam Wolfe/Special To The State) Michael Sauls Thu, October 29, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads South Carolina football is hitting the road this weekend. Shane Beamer and the Gamecocks will travel to Norman, Oklahoma, on Saturday to face Brent Venables and the Oklahoma Sooners. The SEC matchup is set to kick off at 4:15 and will be televised on SEC Network. South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) is coming off a big win over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week. Oklahoma beat Mississippi State last week on the road. The Gamecocks and Sooners have played just twice in the all-time series. South Carolina beat Oklahoma on the road in 2024 and the Sooners beat the Gamecocks last year in Columbia. Here's what you need to know about Saturday's game: Is South Carolina vs. Oklahoma football game on TV? Who: South Carolina (4-3, 2-3 SEC) vs. Oklahoma (4-3, 2-3 SEC) When: Saturday, Oct. 31 at 4:15 p.m. Where : Memorial Stadium in Norman, Oklahoma Watch: SEC Network Stream: ESPN app or ESPN.com Broadcast crew: Taylor Zarzour, Gene Chizik, Michella Chester Local radio crew: Todd Ellis, Tommy Suggs, Chet Tucker Satellite radio: Sirius XM Channel 176 or 229 (953 on app) Series history: Tied 1-1 (Oklahoma won last matchup in 2025) South Carolina vs. Oklahoma betting odds Despite pulling off back-to-back ranked upsets, and being favored over then-No. 11 Tennessee last week, South Carolina is an underdog this week. Oklahoma opened as a 5.5-point favorite, according to the VegasInsider consensus . That line has since moved a bit and the Sooners are now favored by 4.5 points by major sportsbooks such as FanDuel and DraftKings. South Carolina is 3-4 against the spread this year. ESPN Analytics also favors the Sooners. ESPN gives South Carolina a 36.1% chance of winning the game. Injury updates South Carolina had seven players listed on the official SEC injury report released Wednesday night. WR Jayden Sellers, edge rusher Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josian Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. Sellers and Thompson are both out for the year. DB Quay'sheed Scott and RB Jawarn Howell are both listed as doubtful. Scott has missed the last two games. Howell was out last week vs. Tennessee. The SEC injury report will be updated on Thursday, Friday and 90 minutes before kickoff on Saturday. Weather forecast for the game in Norman If you're making the trip to Oklahoma this weekend, be sure to pack an umbrella and a jacket. Temperatures aren't expected to surpass 64 degrees and will dip into the mid-50s. There will be thick cloud cover with a touch of rain, per Accuweather's 10-day forecast. There's a 55% chance of rain all day Saturday for the Norman area. Top storylines Three's a streak: A win over Oklahoma on Saturday would give South Carolina its third straight win. The Gamecocks haven't won three consecutive SEC games since they ended the 2024 season with four straight SEC wins. That six-game winning streak to close out the 2024 season was also the last time the Gamecocks won three games in a row. Should USC beat Oklahoma, it would get the Gamecocks' SEC record back to .500. Sellers needs help in the run game: Make no mistake, South Carolina still has the No. 1 rushing offense in the SEC. The Gamecocks are averaging 218 yards per game, but things haven't looked perfect in recent weeks. Anyone not named LaNorris Sellers has had trouble consistently running the ball for South Carolina. Sellers has accounted for 313 of the 480 rushing yards the Gamecocks have compiled in the last three games. That's certainly good, but USC's running backs need to get going so all the pressure isn't on Sellers' legs down the stretch. Ranking on the horizon? South Carolina received votes in both the Associated Press Top 25 and USA Today Coaches Poll this week after beating Tennessee. USC received 12 votes from the coaches and eight votes from the media. Will a win over Oklahoma be enough to catapult USC into the national rankings for the first time since September 2025? Only time will tell. South Carolina and Oklahoma players to watch South Carolina K Malik Orsan: The sophomore was South Carolina's savior last week. Orsan drilled a 48-yard field goal to help the Gamecocks beat then-No. 11 Tennessee 27-24 as the clock expired. The Southeast Missouri State transfer wasn't necessarily considered to be the top kicker on the roster during USC's kicking competition this offseason. But he's quickly proven why he won the starting job by going 10 for 12 on field goal attempts and 22 for 22 on extra-point attempts this season. South Carolina OL Nolan Hay: The fifth-year offensive lineman was named the Outland Trophy National Player of the Week on Tuesday by the Football Writers Association of America. Hay has been one of the best offensive linemen for the Gamecocks this year. He typically starts at guard but has played some center in Carter Miller's absence because of injury. Hay's Pro Football Focus blocking grade is one of the best on the team. Oklahoma QB John Mateer: There was some buzz around Mateer's name this offseason, but he's found himself in a bit of a rut in 2026. Mateer has thrown for 1,591 yards and 11 touchdowns but has also thrown seven interceptions. He's got a strong arm and is capable of using his legs in the ground game, but has been generally turnover-prone this season. Oklahoma WR Isaiah Sategna III: Sategna was an All-SEC player last year after finishing with 965 receiving yards. The fifth-year student has been Mateer's favorite target in 2026. Sategna leads Oklahoma with 41 catches and 578 yards.

While the Gamecocks aren't ranked, they are surging right now, coming off huge victories at Florida and at home against Tennessee . Those 2 galvanizing wins followed 3 straight losses that threatened to sink South Carolina's season, but the Gamecocks (4-3, 2-3 SEC) have come roaring back through the middle of the season and now will look to make it 3 wins in a row on Saturday. picks.headline: Clemson Tigers vs Florida State Seminoles Preview & Start Time — October 31, 2026 | SI
ESPN predicts the winner of Clemson football vs. Florida State
picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 3-2 ACC) is coming off a last-minute 20-16 loss to the Virginia Tech Hokies at Memorial Stadium. The Tigers led for much of the second half, but Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer led his team on an 11-play, 69-yard drive for the game-winning score with 1:44 to play. Grunkmeyer's 5-yard touchdown pass to tight end Luke Reynolds on fourth-and-1 gave Virginia Tech its first win over Clemson in 19 years and dropped the Tigers to 2-8 in their last 10 home games against Power Four opponents. The offense struggled once again, netting only 288 total yards and going 3 of 14 on third downs. Freshman QB Tait Reynolds completed 20 of his 26 passes, but his average completion went for only 5.9 yards. The Tigers rank dead last in the ACC and just 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game. Clemson will face a Florida State (3-4, 1-3) team fresh off a bye, and one that should be playing with plenty of confidence. Mike Norvell's Seminoles took the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes into double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 17. Fifth-year senior Ashton Daniels leads the Seminoles' passing attack and has 1,618 yards and 12 touchdowns to eight interceptions in seven games this season. Daniels threw four touchdown passes and rushed for another score in FSU's loss to Miami in Week 7. Clemson has won nine of the last 10 meetings against Florida State dating back to 2015. Will the Tigers' run of dominance in the rivalry continue or end Saturday in Tallahassee? Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Florida State as a 6.5-point favorite over Clemson, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. picks.blurb: Clemson (4-3, 2-2 ACC) and Florida State (3-4, 1-3), which have played every year since 1992 with the exception of 2020, are both at a crossroads. Neither program wants to move on from its coach and pay a hefty buyout, but neither team has shown very much on the field lately to offer hope. The Tigers suffered a 20-16 gut-punch loss to Virginia Tech in Week 8. It marked Clemson's eighth in its last 10 games against a Power Four opponent at home. The Tigers led for much of the second half until Ethan Grunkemeyer's game-winning 5-yard touchdown pass on fourth-and-1 with 1:44 left. Florida State came within a play or two of adding to the chaos that was college football's thrilling Week 7 slate. The Seminoles took Miami to double overtime before falling 43-35 at Hard Rock Stadium. FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels accounted for five touchdowns in the loss, including four through the air. Clemson hasn't thrown four touchdowns all season. Tait Reynolds, the 19-year-old true freshman who was thrust into the starting job following an injury to Christopher Vizzina, is averaging just 6.1 yards per completion and has been sacked 20 times in seven games behind a weak offensive line. Clemson ranks 115th nationally in total offense with 333.1 yards per game, which is last in the ACC. Florida State ranks 49th with 414.3 total yards per games. Here's ESPN's prediction for Saturday's game. Will Clemson football beat Florida State? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Florida State, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Seminoles winning their first game against the Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium since 2014. The oddsmakers' latest 5.5 spread favors FSU, as well. Connelly's final score prediction: Florida State 27, Clemson 24. He gives the Seminoles a win probability of 59%. Where Clemson, Florida State sit in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 9 rivalry Clemson is No. 55 in ESPN's SP+ team rankings , up one spot from last week despite the loss to Virginia Tech. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.7, up from 4.0 a week ago. Clemson is one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's overall team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.3 rating on offense (No. 97 nationally, up one spot from last week) and a 19.0 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is the same as before the Tigers' loss to the Hokies. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.5 rating, which ranks 10th-best in the nation. Florida State is No. 54 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 5.8, one spot below Virginia and one ahead of Clemson. The metrics give the Seminoles a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 32 nationally, a 27.1 rating on defense that's No. 76, and a 0.2 rating in special teams that's 43rd in the country. What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." "SP+ is not a résumé ranking, so it does not automatically give credit for big wins or particularly brave scheduling -- no good predictive system does," he adds. picks.blurb: Clemson Predicted to Drop Another Game vs Florida State This Week ClemsonRoundtable 144 Members • 1,122 Posts ClemsonRoundtable ClemsonRoundtable Related stories Trending stories Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network South Ca Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network South Ca Clemson Predicted to Drop Another Game vs Florida State This Week Matt Levine Partner Oct 29, 2026 7:43 PM Published Oct 29, 2026 7:43 PM The Clemson Tigers could be in some trouble this weekend. The Clemson Tigers will be heading out on the road for a big game against the Florida State Seminoles this week. Clemson comes into the contest with a record of 4-3 on the season, having lost last week to Virginia Tech. Florida State will be entering the game with a record of 3-4 for the season, looking to defend home field this week. In a new prediction from college football analyst David Kenyon of Bleacher Report , Clemson will struggle in this game against Florida State. Kenyon has the Tigers dropping the game to the Seminoles by a score of 24-19. If this prediction were to come true, it would send the Tigers into some real trouble, with them falling to 4-4 on the season. There have already been calls for head coach Dabo Swinney to be let go of before the year started, and if the team can't turn things around, it will only grow louder. Related stories For Clemson to avoid dropping the game to Florida State, the offense is going to have to get going. The Tigers have been carried by their defense all season long, with the offensive attack falling way behind. Quarterback Tait Reynolds has struggled in his first action in college, and he has limited what this Tigers team can do. For the year, Reynolds has thrown for just 1,096 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Reynolds has seen problems trying to push the ball down the field, and the offense has been ineffective due to this. Clemson has to find some sort of footing offensively if they want to take down Florida State on the road this week. Due to the struggles of Reynolds, there have been calls for the Tigers to make a switch at the quarterback position. But for now, Swinney seems content to go with Reynolds, even though he had previously said that a change could be made. Christopher Vizzina entered the year as the starter, but was then benched after just two weeks for Reynolds. Vizzina did suffer an injury, but he has remained on the bench due to performance, according to Swinney. If the Tigers were to drop this game to the Seminoles, the calls for Vizzina to return would likely continue. Swinney would then have some choices to make, especially with the season starting to spiral out of control for the team. Kickoff for the game between the Tigers and Seminoles is scheduled for 4:00 p.m. PT/7:00 p.m. ET from Doak S. Campbell Stadium.

Florida State has a completely decimated backfield and an offense that is desperate to find playmakers at any position. Help is truly needed, and a healthy Carter might be able to do so, but now the question is whether or not that impact will be felt against Clemson. With limited options left on offense, Florida State is going to have to change a few things around against Clemson, starting with how the team attacks. Ousmane Kromah and Samuel Singleton Jr. are both out, meaning the team is down to just three healthy running backs, including two who have barely played at the collegiate level. Nobody in the receiving room has truly stepped up this season consistently, and that is a problem that the Seminoles need to shake without either starting running back available. No shade to Amari Thomas or Tre Wisner at all, but replicating the consistency and success of Ousmane Kromah is difficult to do, even with two players. Something has got to give, and either Florida State finds ways to attack through the air or the team sends Thomas and Wisner straight into walls of defenders. This is where Carter comes into play, as a fresh new receiver who was exciting throughout camp, making plays that even the experienced receivers struggled to make. It is hard to imagine Carter triumphing in his collegiate debut, but Florida State needs someone to take the lead, and the freshman has all of the tools to do so. Part of the issues Florida State has had through the air this season can be attributed to quarterback Ashton Daniels, who struggles at times to accurately push the football through the air. home.headline: Florida State injury updates: Mike Norvell expects key returns, but timing is an issue
home.blurb: Florida State coach Mike Norvell recently provided a couple of injury updates on multiple Seminoles who have missed significant time this season. Injuries have been a huge issue for the team this year for Norvell, particularly on defense, where multiple players are out for the season. Sometimes injuries can make or break a team, and so far, the Seminoles have been able to do quite a bit with multiple contributors sidelined. Norvell kicked off his injury updates portion of the press conference with a quick tidbit on linebacker Blake Nichelson, who has not played since the season opener against New Mexico State. Nichelson is nearing a return, and while the game against Clemson might still be out of reach , the linebacker should be able to return to play soon. Samuel Singleton Jr.'s return would be huge for the Florida State offense Norvell is not giving up on Singleton's return; he never ruled the running back out for the season, and he clearly still thinks there is hope for his return. It might be a delusion at this point from Norvell to avoid the reality that Florida State is in a bad spot at running back, or a future return this season might still truly be in the cards. I personally would like to think that Singleton is close to coming back, and the faster he can return, the better for Florida State. Tre Wisner is an experienced running back, but he has not been the most effective player in a short sample size this season. Aside from Wisner, there is not much of an experienced supporting cast. Additionally, Florida State might be in trouble if Singleton is not able to return this season due to the fact that there are only three healthy running backs. The Seminoles truly cannot afford to have another running back go down with an injury, and if Singleton is not available for another two or three weeks, that could be an issue. The timing of Crutchfield's return could not be any better, with Quindarrius Jones, Nehemiah Chandler, and Ashlynd Barker all dealing with injuries. Barker has been playing through his injury thanks to a cast, but Crutchfield can do it all in the secondary, and he should be able to take some pressure off multiple players. You don't start 7-0, score nearly 50 points a game and climb to No. 1 by accident. But there's something about laying more than two touchdowns on the road that makes me uncomfortable, especially against a North Carolina team that's been hanging around with some decent opponents. Miami probably wins this game. I'd be surprised if it didn't. But asking the Hurricanes to go into Chapel Hill and win by 17? That's a different bet altogether. Be ready for all the college football action with our free college football picks . Miami heads to Kenan Memorial Stadium in Chapel Hill on Saturday, October 31, 2026. Kickoff is set for 7:30 PM ET on ABC. The Hurricanes opened as 14.5-point favorites, with some books now showing 15.5. Our original betting numbers were North Carolina +16.5 and Under 51.5. That extra point on the spread matters, and I wouldn't pretend every sportsbook is still offering it. This is an outdoor game, so I'll want another look at the Chapel Hill weather forecast before kickoff, particularly the wind and any chance of rain. Miami Hurricanes Have the Offense to Put This Away Early Miami is 7-0, including 3-0 away from home, and just beat Pittsburgh 52-23. The Hurricanes have scored 43 or more in three of their last four games, and they've already beaten Clemson 41-13 on the road. That's a pretty good argument for laying the points, I'll give you that. Pittsburgh couldn't do much with Miami's passing game Saturday. The Hurricanes scored 52, and the scary part is that they still left some plays out there. North Carolina isn't going to survive if it spends the first half giving Miami short fields and easy touchdowns. The numbers explain why the Hurricanes are such a big favorite. They're averaging 49 points and 552 yards per game. Nobody in the country is producing more total offense. Miami throws for about 341 yards a game and runs for another 211, so taking away one part of the offense doesn't necessarily solve anything. Defensively, the Hurricanes allow just 15.3 points and 60 rushing yards per game. Sixty. That's going to make life difficult for a North Carolina offense that hasn't run the ball particularly well. Miami also converts 54.5% of its third downs. If the Tar Heels can't get the Hurricanes off the field, that home crowd won't have much to cheer about. He's thrown for 2,151 yards with 22 touchdowns and just one interception, completing better than 81% of his passes. Against Pittsburgh, he went 31-for-37 for 387 yards and four scores. Malachi Toney caught 16 passes for 194 yards and three touchdowns in that game, giving him 952 receiving yards and 11 touchdowns on the season. Javian Mallory has added 444 rushing yards and seven touchdowns. That's plenty of offense for North Carolina to worry about. Miami does have some injuries, with receiver Jalen Moore and running back Chris Brown out for the season. Tight end Logan Gilbert is also sidelined, while Owen Ruskavich's status needs checking. But the Hurricanes haven't had much trouble scoring without them. North Carolina Tar Heels Need to Make Miami Earn Everything North Carolina is 4-3 overall and 1-2 at home. The Tar Heels had won two straight before losing 31-30 to Syracuse in overtime Saturday. That one had to sting. They had a chance to get their fifth win and instead let Syracuse walk out of Chapel Hill with it. Still, I wouldn't throw out everything North Carolina has done because of one ugly finish. The Tar Heels beat Pittsburgh 21-17 on the road and followed it with a 24-20 win at Duke. They also played Clemson to an eight-point game. Those aren't the results of a team that rolls over every time it sees a better opponent. The offense is the problem. North Carolina averages 24.4 points and 336 yards per game, and the running game produces only 114 yards a night. That's not much help against Miami's defensive front. The Tar Heels are probably going to have to throw more than they'd like. Defensively, though, they've allowed 20.9 points per game. That's respectable, even if the 373 yards they're giving up tells you opponents are moving the ball. What worries me most is third down. North Carolina allows opponents to convert 43.1% of the time. Miami is one of the best third-down teams in the country. That's a bad matchup, and Bill Belichick has to find a way to get his defense off the field before the Hurricanes start piling up possessions. Billy Edwards Jr. has thrown for 1,530 yards with 11 touchdowns and five interceptions. He passed for 271 yards and two scores against Syracuse, so he can move the ball when he gets protection. Jordan Shipp has 543 receiving yards, including eight catches for 102 yards and a touchdown Saturday. Benjamin Hall leads the running backs with 283 yards, while Demon June has seven rushing touchdowns. The Tar Heels are dealing with some injuries at receiver, including Carnell Warren and Kaden Chapman, and they're missing tight ends Jordan Washington and Jake Warren. That's not ideal when you're facing a defense as good as Miami's. But Edwards has enough experience to keep North Carolina from becoming completely one-dimensional. Miami vs North Carolina Picks and Predictions North Carolina Tar Heels +16.5 I'm taking North Carolina +16.5, assuming that number is still available. I know Miami could make this look foolish in a hurry. The Hurricanes have the better quarterback, the better offense and a defense that barely lets anybody run the ball. But sixteen and a half points is a lot to lay on the road against a team that's been competitive with Clemson, Pittsburgh and Duke. North Carolina has lost three games, and two of those defeats came by eight points or fewer. The Tar Heels also have a quarterback who can throw well enough to put together a late scoring drive if they're down a couple of touchdowns. That's what I'm looking for here. Miami can control most of the game and still fail to cover a number this big. I wouldn't be surprised by a 30-17 or 34-20 Miami win. Either one gets the job done for North Carolina backers at +16.5. At +14.5, though, I like it considerably less. I'll take Under 51.5, although this is the pick that makes me a little nervous. Miami is averaging 49 points a game by itself, and that's not something you can just ignore. But North Carolina isn't built to get into a scoring contest with the Hurricanes. The Tar Heels need to run some clock, avoid turnovers and make Miami work for its points. They can't afford to turn this into a game where both teams are snapping the ball every twenty seconds. Miami's defense should help us here because the Hurricanes allow only 15.3 points per game and have been excellent against the run. If North Carolina finishes somewhere around 14 or 17 points, Miami can score into the low 30s without pushing this over. The danger is an early Miami explosion or a couple of defensive touchdowns. That's real. But I think the Tar Heels will try to slow the game down, and Miami's defense should keep North Carolina from doing too much scoring. Give me Miami 31-17. Miami announced the look on Thursday, pairing white helmets with white jerseys and white pants (the program's standard road uniform). The No. 1 Hurricanes are undefeated in the combination this season after road wins at Stanford (45-6), Wake Forest (33-20) and Clemson (41-13). All white, all business 🙌 pic.twitter.com/dpVbfdILLx North Carolina enters at 4-3 overall and 2-2 in ACC play, while Miami (7-0, 5-0 ACC) arrives as a two-touchdown favorite. The Hurricanes are seeking their first win in Chapel Hill since 2017 and first victory in the series since 2018. North Carolina has won the past five meetings and holds a series edge 16-11. The Hurricanes have largely stuck to a simple rotation. The all-white Stormtroopers have served as the primary road look, and at home they have worn the traditional white helmet, orange jersey and white pants combination against Florida A&M and Florida State. The green alternate (white helmet, green jersey, green pants) appeared once, in a 52-3 win over Central Michigan. Sayin, who threw for 2,007 yards and 19 touchdowns this season, is expected to be out indefinitely. Who's on deck for the Buckeyes? As of Thursday, both freshman Luke Fahey and redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair were preparing to play against USC. It's among the most super of superpowers. It's one of those programs with no excuses. It gets just about any player it wants, its realistic expectations are national title or bust, and it's one of the few programs that can lose its starting quarterback and still reasonably be considered the No. 1 team in the country. But now it has to go at least the next several weeks without star quarterback Julian Sayin, who injured his shoulder in the win over Indiana a few weeks ago. There's a quarterback battle to see who steps into the role as the team travels to Los Angeles to face a desperate USC team in a whole lot of trouble. The Trojans are 6-2, but they just got stuffed by Wisconsin in a punishing 24-7 loss, and with a brutal schedule to close, the Lincoln Riley hot seat is flaming. On the plus side, win, and the team is still deep in the College Football Playoff hunt. Ohio State vs USC: Quick Hits It doesn't get any easier for USC with a trip to Indiana next after a week off, and then Maryland, and it all closes at UCLA. Ohio State finishes with three of its last four games in Columbus, hosting Oregon next week. The road game is at Nebraska. This is the first time these two have met since a 24-7 Ohio State win in the 2017 Cotton Bowl. USC has won seven or the last eight in the series goning back to the 1974 Rose Bowl. It has a wonderful 6-2 record, quarterback Jayden Maiava is terrific, and there's still pop and explosion to worry about, but there are flaws. It beat Washington and Penn State, but lost at home to a struggling Oregon, and couldn't get anything going against the Badgers. Ohio State isn't the Ohio State of previous seasons, but it's still good enough to beat anyone else this year. To win, the Buckeyes have to screw up, but USC doesn't take the ball away with just six turnovers forced on the season, and there's little running game to worry about. USC ran well on Rutgers and Louisiana, and that's about it. Slow down the midrange USC passing game, slow down USC. Why USC Will Win If Ohio State didn't exactly go turn-it-loose full-throttle with Julian Sayin under center, what will it do with Luke Fahey and/or Tavien St. Clair? Both are talented prospects, and no matter who is under center, there's still Jeremiah Smith and a loaded receiving corps to throw to, but this is where the offense has to rely on the running game, and it might not be able to do it. The Buckeyes are averaging a pedestrian four yards per carry, and were stuffed by Indiana two weeks ago, gaining just 37 yards. Fahey missed both of his throws against Indiana, and St. Clair has only seen the lightest of mop-up work so far. Ohio State vs USC Prediction, Betting Lines Which team has another gear? Can USC's run defense ball out, and can Jayden Maiava play like the best quarterback on the field? Or will the Ohio State defense step up and keep the big pass plays to a minimum? Yes, Indiana came within a few inches from beating Ohio State, but Josh Hoover only hit 50% of his passes, and only Arch Manning has been able to complete more than 56% against the Buckeyes. Maiava will have a nice day, but the Trojans will stall a bit too often. It won't be pretty, but the Buckeyes will take advantage of a few good field position chances to survive and advance in a relatively low-scoring game. ESPN predicts winner of Ohio State football vs. USC Saturday night Phil Harrison, Buckeyes Wire Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:05 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After enjoying a week off to heal and to figure out a game plan for replacing injured starting quarterback Julian Sayin , Ohio State travels out west to Los Angeles for a road game against Big Ten foe USC . It's a collision between two teams that still have some pretty big goals on the table, and despite the Buckeyes facing breaking in a new quarterback away from home, Vegas has the Buckeyes as a marginal favorite. With any big game, we like to scour the internet for some predictions, but we also like to tap into ESPN's " matchup predictor " to see what it says about the potential winner of the game, and there's no reason to stop now. ESPN uses analytics to determine the percentage chance of each team winning, and in this case, it has Ohio State with a whopping 82.8% chance of leaving the Coliseum still undefeated in the Big Ten. But that's why they play the games, right? Since these analytics are updated by game results only, there's no chance of this percentage changing, but the Buckeyes will still need to execute at a high level and take their defense on the road. The game is set to kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC, and we'll have more on the game leading up to Saturday, and be around during and after as well for extensive coverage. picks.headline: Know Thy Foe: Baylor Expert Shares What UCF Fans Need To Know For Space Game
picks.blurb: Know Thy Foe: Baylor Expert Shares What UCF Fans Need To Know For Space Game Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL RECRUITING COLLEGE FOOTBALL NEWS Olympic Sports More from UCF Knights On SI FOOTBALL While the UCF Knights may be coming off of one of the most significant wins in its program's history against No. 2 BYU on Saturday, they do not have long before they have to follow it up. The Baylor Bears may be entering their first game of the post-Dave Aranda era after firing him on Sunday, but they still have the same record as the Knights, and their interim coach, Joe Klanderman, has been in charge of a defense that has been one of the top five in the nation in sacks and tackles for loss. Jacob Haddaadin is both a Baylor graduate and a contributor for Baylor Bears on SI, and he took some time this week to answer some of our questions about the Bears (4-3, 2-2 Big 12): 1. How did the Bears reach a position in which they ended up firing their head coach midseason? Haddadin: Dave Aranda’s firing wasn't strictly due to this season's results. Ever since Dave Aranda won the Big 12 championship in 2021, the program has slowly trended downward. The Bears had real momentum after beating ASU in Tempe, but that momentum stalled after a double-digit home loss to TCU and a loss to a bad Kansas team in Lawrence. Dave Aranda had a losing record in the Big 12, a 1-6 record against rival TCU, and his teams were consistently unprepared in big games. We are forever grateful for the 12-2 season in 2021, but enough was enough, and Baylor fans were fed up with the constant expectation and disappointment cycle that was Dave Aranda. The loss to Kansas solidified that the Dave Aranda-led team was once again not going to be anything special. Cementing his exit from the program. 2. What’s the rundown on interim coach Joe Klanderman? What made him the choice to lead the program for the remainder of the season? Haddadin: Before Manhattan, Klanderman cut his teeth at North Dakota State, where he spent five years as defensive backs coach from 2014 to 2018, contributing to four FCS national championships. He then spent seven years at Kansas State, six of them running the defense, and K-State maintained a top-30 national ranking in defensive efficiency for five straight seasons through 2025. Part of what made him the choice is continuity. He was brought to Waco as one of the big offseason moves meant to turn things around; he’s already in the building, and the defense he built has been the most reliable part of this team. He has also come in with a clear plan, laying out three priorities for his time as interim head coach: energizing the program, strengthening the roster for 2027, and establishing complementary football to help Baylor win more games. He has been honest about where the problems are, too, pointing to the offensive line and the running game as the areas that need the most work. Whether or not this turns into a permanent job, the next five games give him a real chance to make his case, starting with a Friday night road game at UCF. 3. Quarterback DJ Lagway seems to have really connected with wide receiver Gavin Freeman, the latter of which is second in the nation in receptions per game and 14th in the nation in receiving yards. What makes Freeman such an oft-target wideout? Also, is there anyone else in the Bears’ receiving corps that could step up as a main target if Freeman is well-covered? Haddadin: Gavin Freeman’s production makes sense once you look at what he brings. At 5-9 and 189 pounds, he isn’t going to win many jump balls, but he has been reliable all season. He arrived as a redshirt senior after playing 2022-23 at Oklahoma and 2024-25 at Oklahoma State, and he was already a go-to receiver before coming to Waco, leading the Cowboys with 53 receptions for 481 yards and four scores in 2025. His fit with Lagway was clear from the first game, when he caught 12 passes for 154 yards and a touchdown in his Baylor debut against Auburn. It also helps that during the offseason, observers expected the passing game to work the middle of the field more, since Lagway is more comfortable there than Sawyer Robertson was. That is exactly where a quick, shifty slot receiver like Freeman does his best work. He has also produced when the offense hasn’t: in the 17-6 loss to TCU, he still caught seven passes for 76 yards. He adds value in other ways too. Last year at Oklahoma State, he contributed in both the passing and running game and as a returner. If defenses focus on Freeman, the most likely next option is Louis Brown IV. Before the season, he was described as the leader of the receiver room as one of its few upperclassmen with real experience in the offense, and he and Lagway connected well in the spring. Jadon Porter is another option to watch, and Baylor’s tight ends have been factors in the red zone. 4. Baylor is one of the most penalized teams in the Big 12. Is there one side of the ball that draws more flags? If so, why? Also, is there a particular penalty that gets called a lot? Haddadin: Most of the flags come from the offense, and specifically the offensive line. Through the early home stretch, one count found that the offense was outpacing the defense by nearly 3 to 1 in total penalties. The penalty that keeps showing up is the false start. Baylor had 5 against Prairie View A&M, 3 against Louisiana Tech, and 3 against Colorado, for at least 11 false starts in three home games. The Prairie View game was the low point: all four of Baylor’s false-start penalties were attributed to offensive lineman Asher Hale, and Aranda admitted afterward that one player had a bunch of penalties. Holding calls have added to the problem, but false starts are harder to excuse. ​A big reason is inexperience. The line was overhauled in the offseason and has been banged up in 2026, and while Baylor has capable players at each spot, most are new and started their first games together this year. Injuries haven’t helped either, including the injury to Koltin Sieracki, who was projected to be the best of the bunch but has not produced on the level the staff or fans expected. 5. The Bears have had a knack for getting behind the line of scrimmage this season, ranking in the top five in the nation in both sacks and tackles for loss. Who do they have to thank for that and what helps them get past offensive lines so often this season? Haddadin: The turnaround is remarkable given where this defense was a year ago. Baylor finished last season tied for last in the Big 12 and at the bottom of the FBS in sacks. Much of the credit goes to Klanderman and an offseason rebuild that put NIL money into the roster from the inside out. Defensive end Garrick Ponder leads the team with 3.5 sacks, Ryan Davis has added 2.5 off the edge, and Jordan Mack has chipped in 2.0. Up the middle, Hosea Wheeler and Traevon Mitchell occupy blockers and collapse the pocket, which opens lanes for everyone else. The most telling detail may be that two of the top three sack producers are safeties: Bo Onu and Daniel Cobbs have 3.0 sacks apiece. That says a lot about how Klanderman calls a game. He isn’t relying on one star pass rusher; six different players have at least two sacks, and he is willing to bring pressure from anywhere on the field, including the secondary. 6. What’s an aspect of this Bears team’s game that is not talked about enough? ​Haddadin: The most underrated part of this team might be the guy who comes on when the offense stalls. Senior punter Palmer Williams has quietly been one of the best weapons on the roster. He came into the year with plenty of credentials, as a 2025 All-American and Ray Guy Award finalist who earned first-team Walter Camp and second-team AP preseason All-American honors before this season. He picked up right where he left off. In the opener against Auburn, he punted four times for 208 yards, a 52-yard average, and earned Ray Guy Award Punter of the Week honors for flipping field position and helping Baylor get back into a game it nearly stole at the end. A month into the season, he was averaging over 50 yards a punt and consistently pinning punts near the goal line. He was a massive part of the win against Colorado in Week 4. As the offense struggled to move the ball, Williams flipped the field and pinned the Buffs inside their own 10-yard line on multiple occasions. If Friday’s game against UCF turns into a cagey field-position battle, Baylor won’t mind, since it has one of the best punters in the country. Turner has contributed to the Black and Gold Banneret, the home for UCF Athletics on SB Nation. He has called the Orlando area home since the age of 8 and received his bachelor's and master's degrees from UCF. Baylor vs UCF Prediction: Who Can Build Off the Moment? Pete Fiutak Thu, October 29, 2026 at 2:02 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here's the punchline – both Baylor and UCF are 4-3 overall and 2-2 in Big 12 play. On one side, Baylor lost on the road to Kansas in a 25-24 fight, and that was it. Head coach Dave Aranda was fired, defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman is the interim head man, and the team needs this win with a tough November coming up. However, win in Orlando, beat Iowa State at home, and boom – the Bears are bowl-eligible. UCF lost on the road to Houston and Oklahoma State, and then it changed the national landscape – and got Scott Frost his first huge win in his second round with the Knights – with a 39-31 victory over BYU. With a very favorable finishing kick, UCF has to keep the momentum going. Baylor vs UCF: Quick Hits Baylor has the home date against Iowa State next, and then there's a problem – at BYU, Texas Tech, at Houston. UCF goes to Kansas after this, and then plays Arizona State, Iowa State, and goes to Colorado. None of those four are likely to go to a bowl game. It's the fourth meeting between the two. Baylor won 30-3 last year and won 36-35 in 2023, but UCF won a wild 52-42 Fiesta Bowl to end the 2013 season. How To Watch Baylor vs UCF Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando, FL – Week 9 Schedule, Game Previews – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Predicting the First CFP Top 25 – CFN Week 9 Expert Picks Why Baylor Will Win The defense is taking the ball away in bunches. The run defense has been fantastic – Kansas ripped it up last week, but that was an anomaly – but the takeaways have been the biggest help, with 13 overall and at least two in four games. UCF doesn't have to get the running game going to win, but it's a huge help going 4-1 when running for more than 100 yards. Baylor has held four teams to under 100, but … Why UCF Will Win UCF isn't having a problem with turnovers. It has only given it up seven times, didn't turn it over against BYU, and it's +5 overall in turnover margin. So really, how did UCF beat BYU? The running game was effective enough – even if it wasn't dominant – and the passing game was fearless, and that's how the Knights have to play. They don't have to bomb away, but they should take the midrange plays against a Baylor pass defense that can get to the quarterback but is susceptible to quick hits. Baylor vs UCF Prediction, Betting Lines UCF needs to capitalize on the momentum, and it will. The Knights are 4-0 in the Bounce House, and 0-3 away from it. Baylor hung 55 at Arizona State and suffered two one-point losses away from Waco, but now it has to deal with the coaching drama and all the changes. The team will play hard and well for Klanderman, but the UCF offense will be just a bit more effective. picks.blurb: 2026 Week 9 Space Game Preview: Baylor Bears @ UCF Knights - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Packers defeat Panthers WNBA Finals: Dream force Game 7 Bears land DT Jeffery Simmons Brewers win World Series Celebrate, Milwaukee! 2026 Week 9 Space Game Preview: Baylor Bears @ UCF Knights ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights reacts after a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steve Helwick Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:12 PM UTC · 8 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, October 30 at 7:30 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Acrisure Bounce House — Orlando, FL Spread: Baylor (-1.5) Over/under: 48.5 All-time series: Baylor leads, 2-1 Last meeting: Baylor 30, UCF 3 — November 1, 2025 Current streak: Baylor, 2 (2023-25) Setting the scene Baylor and UCF have only met three times, but there is no shortage of iconic moments between these programs. UCF entered the 2013 Fiesta Bowl as a 13.5-point underdog to Big 12 champion Baylor. However, Blake Bortles led the Knights to an electrifying 52-42 victory on New Year's Day, sealing the program's first-ever AP Top 10 finish. Ten years later, UCF held a 35-7 lead in the late third quarter over Baylor, but the Bears rallied with 29 unanswered, surviving a wild fourth down conversion and a 59-yard field goal attempt to hold onto a 36-35 win. Perhaps another memorable finish awaits as the programs meet in Orlando for the 10th annual Space Game. UCF continues one of college football's most recognizable modern traditions, rebranding to the "Citronauts" for a night and donning space-themed alternate uniforms as a nod to the university's aeronautical roots. The Citronauts are one of the better teams in college football history, owning an 8-1 record in Space Games and outscoring opponents by an aggregate result of 432-189: 2017 – UCF 63, East Carolina 21 2018 – UCF 52, Temple 40 2019 – UCF 44, Houston 29 2020 – UCF 51, Tulane 34 2021 – UCF 24, Memphis 7 2022 – UCF 70, Temple 13 2023 – UCF 45, Oklahoma State 3 2024 – UCF 56, Arizona 12 2025 – Houston 30, UCF 27 However, Houston defeated UCF in last year's Space Game, spoiling the Citronauts' perfect record. UCF, coming off its first top-5 victory in program history, aims to recapture its galactic momentum as Baylor strolls into the Bounce House. Baylor Bears outlook WACO, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 19: Defensive Coordinator Joe Klanderman of the Baylor Bears yells from the sideline during the second quarter during the game against the Louisiana Tech Bulldogs on September 19, 2026 at the McLane Stadium in Waco, Texas. (Photo by Hanna Kotlarek/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Baylor (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) fired head coach Dave Aranda in the middle of his seventh season in Waco. Aranda's tenure was quite volatile, featuring highs of a 12-2 finish and Big 12 championship in 2021, but lows including a 3-9 record in 2023. The Bears lacked consistency under Aranda, improving or declining by at least three wins in every year from 2019 through 2025. Baylor moves forward with interim Joe Klanderman, who also retains his defensive coordinator duties. In year one on campus, Klanderman has done a stellar job reforming Baylor's defense. He implemented a 3-3-5 base scheme and vastly improved the unit, allowing them to skyrocket from 122nd to 19th in scoring defense and 122nd to 22nd in run defense. The Bears let up just 16.1 points per game, and last Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas was the first time they surrendered more than 17 points all season. The defense showed promise even in losing efforts, falling 17-16 to Auburn and 17-6 to TCU. Baylor is the best in the Big 12 at getting to the quarterback and its 3.9 sacks per game rank third nationally. There isn't one dominant pass rusher, rather, it's a concerted effort. Edge rusher Garrick Ponder leads the charge with 4.0 sacks while safeties Daniel Cobbs and Bo Onu are tied for second with 3.0 apiece. With great pressure comes great chaos, and Baylor is producing takeaways at a high rate. The team ranks 15th nationally with 13 takeaways, and strong safety Micah Gifford has been omnipresent with three interceptions and two fumble recoveries. While the passing defense has more interceptions than touchdowns allowed, and forces opponents to a 59.8 completion rate, Baylor still allows 236 passing yards per game, which ranks 103rd nationally. Teams regularly hit explosives on the Bears, which have given up 13 passes of 30 yards or greater through seven games. Last season, Baylor excelled offensively and struggled on defense. This year, the opposite is true. Outside of the 55-19 rout at Arizona State, the Bears have not been able to consistently generate points. They scored 24 or fewer points in four of seven games, and all three losses were attribute to a lack of scoring. Still, quarterback DJ Lagway has moved the ball well for the nation's 24th-ranked passing offense. The veteran starter averages 270 passing yards per game, delivering nine touchdowns and four interceptions. Efficiency has been an issue through the air though, and Baylor checks in at 124th in the FBS with a 56.4 completion rate. Wide receiver Gavin Freeman operates as the main target. His 58 receptions are the second-most in the country and his 678 receiving yards rank second in the Big 12. Louis Brown and Jayden McGowan are among Lagway's other frequented options. Baylor hasn't been as lethal on the ground, still awaiting its first 90-yard rusher of the season. The Bears were held to 54 rushing yards against TCU and 122 against Kansas — a significant reason Baylor enters Orlando on a two-game losing streak. UCF Knights outlook ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Keyone Jenkins #12 of the UCF Knights celebrates a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images UCF (4-3, 2-2 Big 12) is coming off a win for the ages. Although the Knights won multiple New Year's Six bowls and secured an NCAA-recognized national championship in 2017, last Saturday's double overtime triumph over No. 2 BYU was the program's first-ever top-5 victory in history. It was the long-awaited signature win of Scott Frost's second tenure in Orlando and restored energy into a fanbase, which will certainly show up in droves for the annual Space Game. There were moments throughout the BYU game where it appeared UCF missed a golden opportunity for an upset. However, the Knights stayed the course and won just their second October game in their last 13 tries. One of the heroes last week was quarterback Keyone Jenkins, who threw for 293 yards and three touchdowns, while rushing for an additional score in the 39-31 win. After witnessing several strong performances by the FIU transfer, Frost named Jenkins the starting quarterback moving forward, even though original starter Alonza Barnett III has recovered from a Week 2 hamstring injury. UCF has received stronger support from the passing attack in recent weeks, which has been efficient. The Knights have thrown 13 touchdowns against four interceptions, while completing 66.5 percent of attempts this year. It hasn't been the most explosive unit, completing just seven passes spanning 30 yards and two spanning 40, but Jenkins has allowed the Knights to piece together methodical possessions. The run game has been the hallmark of UCF's offense all season. Running back Duke Watson is eighth in the Big 12 in rushing and averages 6.8 yards per carry. Landen Chambers has also stepped up from the backfield lately, scoring two touchdowns in last week's win over BYU. But the true emerging star in UCF's offense is true freshman wide receiver Tyren Hornes. After being underutilized in September, Hornes has become one of the top options for the Knights, producing 137 yards on six receptions last Saturday. He now ranks second on the team in receiving yards behind Josh Derry, who leads all Knight receivers in catches (34), yards (358), and touchdowns (3). Although the last two weeks were more offensive oriented games, UCF has been best on the defensive side this year. The Knights allow 23.0 points per game, allow just 3.2 yards per rushing attempt, and hold opponents to a completion rate of 58.9 percent. However, UCF must play the Space Game without arguably its best defensive player. Strong safety Demari Henderson suffered an injury in overtime against BYU, and the team will miss his production, which includes 35 tackles, two interceptions, and five pass breakups. The Knights still have several veteran faces in the secondary including cornerbacks Antione Jackson and Jayden Bellamy, who both have one interception and one forced fumble on the season. Thanks to these defensive backs, UCF is a plus-5 in the turnover battle this season. Can UCF avoid a letdown after an emotional win? Signature wins haven't been easy to follow up in college football this season. Auburn beat Georgia and then lost by 21 to LSU at home. BYU took down Notre Dame and then dropped an overtime thriller to UCF a week later. Ole Miss' triumph over LSU was followed by a thrashing at the hands of Florida. And so on. Baylor also had an eventful week, as the Bears move on from head coach Dave Aranda and now must respond with an interim head coach in a hostile Orlando environment. The Bears' defense has been consistently sound this year, and UCF may struggle to come close to its Space Game average of 48 points per game. The defenses control this matchup, and the Bears prevent a successful launch with a game-winning field goal in the final minute. Prediction: Baylor 24, UCF 21

picks.blurb: Baylor vs. UCF Prediction, Pick and Odds for Week 9 Teams Arizona Wildcats Arizona State Sun Devils Cincinnati Bearcats Colorado Buffaloes Houston Cougars Iowa State Cyclones Kansas Jayhawks Kansas State Wildcats Oklahoma State Cowboys TCU Horned Frogs Texas Tech Red Raiders West Virginia Mountaineers Former Foes Missouri Tigers Nebraska Cornhuskers Oklahoma Sooners Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Recruiting Football Transfer Portal Video Watch on YouTube Listen on Apple Listen on Spotify Forum Members Login Heartland College Sports – An Independent Big 12 Today Blog | College Football News | Big 12 Today The Baylor Bears and UCF Knights kick off Week 9 in the Big 12 on Friday night in Orlando, with both teams coming off dramatically different weekends. UCF enters the game riding high after stunning No. 2 BYU 39-31 in double overtime for the Knights' biggest win since joining the Big 12. Meanwhile, Baylor is beginning a new era after firing head coach Dave Aranda following Saturday's 25-24 loss to Kansas, with defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman taking over as interim head coach. Despite taking very different paths to get here, Baylor and UCF enter Friday night's game with identical 4-3 overall records and 2-2 marks in Big 12 play. For UCF, the question is whether Scott Frost's team can build off its breakthrough win or suffer a letdown. For Baylor, it's about what kind of response the Bears will have in their first game without Aranda. Here is everything you need to know about Baylor vs. UCF in Week 9, including our prediction and pick for Friday night's Big 12 matchup. Baylor vs. UCF Odds Spread: UCF -1.5 Over/Under: 48.5 Moneyline: UCF -120/Baylor +100 Odds as of Tuesday afternoon. Odds are subject to change. The Biggest Question: How do the emotions play a factor? The emotions on both sides of this game are tremendous. UCF is coming off of one of the biggest wins in program history over No. 2 BYU in double overtime at home. Now, they have to put that in the rearview mirror and take on Baylor. What' done is done. Have the Knights spent the last week in celebration mode? And then, on the other side, head coach Dave Aranda was fired on Sunday by Baylor. How does the team respond? How does defensive coordinator Joe Klanderman do in the interim role? There are so many unknowns going into this game, beyond the X's and O's, that ultimately will determine the outcome. Baylor vs. UCF Prediction and Pick Prediction: UCF 23, Baylor 20 It's a short week for both teams, but the good news for UCF is that they're playing their second-straight home game after a bye week. They haven't had to leave the friendly confines of Central Florida in nearly a month. Meantime, Baylor is getting set for its 3rd road game in its last four match ups, and their first without Aranda. In games like this, I try to find a nugget to sway me one way or the other, and here's what I've found: Baylor leads the Big 12 with 27 sacks in seven games. But one of the many things that UCF has done well with Keyone Jenkins is move the pocket, get rid of the ball quickly and avoid pressure in the backfield. BYU only had one sack last week against UCF, and the Knights have only allowed 10 in seven games, good for fourth fewest in the Big 12 Conference. Negating the pass rush by Baylor opens up a lot of opportunities for the UCF offense, and I believe that will be a game-changer on Friday night. Baylor has proven it can play with, and beat, some of the lesser Big 12 teams like Colorado and Arizona State. But even against just slightly better competition, TCU and Kansas, they came up short. UCF is one of the more underrated teams in the country, which I've been telling you since August. And despite their injuries, they're playing solid, team football, and that culminated with a with vs. BYU. But it was not a fluke. They led Houston in the second half on the road. They were beating Oklahoma State in Stillwater early in the game. This team can play with the best. Now, they get a chance to play one of the worst? I'll not overcomplicate this and take UCF to win and cover. Baylor's run defense ranks 4th in the Big 12, but they've already played the three worst running teams in the conference in Colorado, Arizona State and TCU. Now, they get Duke Watson, Jenkins and the rest of the run game going on Friday night to seal a win. UCF wins. UCF covers. first half at McLane Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Raymond Carlin III-Imagn Images College Football Week 9 Friday night college football previews. Baylor vs. UCF Three games are on the college football card for Friday night, headlined by Baylor vs. UCF. Both teams are in very difficult spots here, as the Knights just upset BYU at home in overtime last week and the Bears fired head coach Dave Aranda after losing at home to Kansas. On a night with the MAC, American, and Big 12, we have Kent State as a rare home favorite, a mediocre Tulane team laying double digits, and then the coin flip in Orlando. Despite the tricky circumstances with Baylor and UCF, that’s the game of the night and the game that deserves the most attention. Odds from Circa Sports as of October 28, 1:20 p.m. PT ; check out our Circa Betting Splits and DraftKings Betting Splits . See all of our Week 9 College Football Picks and Predictions . Baylor at UCF (-1, 48) Prediction Friday, 7:30 p.m. ET (ESPN) Baylor invades the Bounce House this week and we’ll see if interim head coach Joe Klanderman can put some more pep in the steps of the Bears. It felt like Aranda was simply holding on for dear life with this gig for a while and it finally came to a head this past week with a blocked field goal that led to a loss against the Jayhawks. I watched Klanderman’s media availability this week and he comes across as a very honest, very poignant guy who isn’t going to BS this team about what’s going on. I appreciate that. In this day and age, I think the players do as well. Klanderman will continue to call the defense, while longtime up-and-comer Jake Spavital has creative freedom on offense. The 41-year-old Spavital was Texas A&M’s OC by the age of 30 and even was Texas State’s head coach for four rough seasons. But he’s always been pretty highly-regarded in the coaching world and now he has free reign of the offense. By no means has the offense been good, but Aranda was kind of a passive guy and there wasn’t a lot of explosiveness or aggressiveness to Baylor’s offensive profile. With a lot of money invested in DJ Lagway, let’s see if Spavital can unlock something. Lagway has only completed 52.1% of his passes and only has 26 carries for 19 yards, so it’s been a struggle to get him free. Leading rusher Dawson Pendergrass only has 3.5 yards per carry. The Baylor offensive line needs to be better, but we should see an improvement in effort and focus for this week. UCF head coach Scott Frost brought in Keyone Jenkins as an insurance policy behind expected starter Alonza Barrett III from James Madison. Instead, it has been Jenkins, the FIU transfer, who has carried this team in Barrett’s absence. He sports an 11/3 TD/INT ratio and a completion rate butting up against 70%, while transfer RB Duke Watson has rushed for 6.8 yards per carry. While Baylor’s defensive numbers stand up a lot better, as the Bears are 17th in the nation in yards per play allowed, it should be noted that Jeff Sagarin has a strength of schedule gap of 30 spots between the two teams, as UCF has already played three top-30 teams per Sagarin and Baylor has not played any. The Knights rank 27th in SOS and the Bears are 57th, with a big difference in Big 12 opponents. UCF has played TCU, Houston, Oklahoma State, and BYU. Baylor has played Colorado, Arizona State, TCU, and Kansas. Of that group, Arizona State is the only one with a winning record and the only one without a losing conference record. It’s a tough spot for UCF coming off of the BYU win, but they aren’t traveling, they don’t have the internal tumult, and Jenkins has definitively outplayed Lagway this season and even done so against better competition. Other Friday Games Tulane (-10, 47) at Charlotte: This is a hefty number for Tulane, a team that ranks 99th with -.51 net points per drive per Brian Fremeau of BCFToys. Of course, Charlotte is 134th out of 138 teams, so we’re talking about one of the worst programs in the nation. The Green Wave have not gotten good QB play out of either Kadin Semonza or Trace Johnson, with 18 total sacks and a 5/5 TD/INT ratio. Even though the Green Wave have a great running game and maybe that will be enough, winning by margin requires taking care of the football and avoiding negative plays. Charlotte has poor run defense numbers, but it should be noted that they’ve allowed 4.55 YPC to FBS opponents and allowed 5.36 YPC in the loss to The Citadel. Kent State (-10, 46.5) at Sacramento State: Historical outliers are scary and Kent State being favored like this on the road hasn’t happened since 2022. That could be part of the reason why we’ve seen money come in on the Hornets and against the Golden Flashes. It’s also just ludicrous to think about Kent State facing these kinds of expectations, but Sac State might be the worst FBS team we’ve ever seen. If Kent wins and covers, that might solidify it, but that’s an enormous ask and the market seems to think it’s too big of one. Frost said he thought Barnett "probably could play," but he did not know if he was 100%. Should he be able to play, he could serve as an emergency backup to Jenkins should he get injured during the game. The Knights' secondary took another hit this week as starting safety Demari Henderson has been ruled out for Friday's Space Game. It will be the first time Henderson has missed a game since he missed a majority of the 2024 season. He joins cornerback DJ Bell , who was ruled out for a second straight week. Maiava was designated as probable and was a game-time decision against BYU, so he is trending towards returning on Friday. Fellow offensive lineman Preston Cushman was also designated probable. Meanwhile, Spell's name is nowhere to be found in Tuesday's report, which could mean one of two things: he is available to play on Friday, or he has been designated out for the season. Frost said back on Sep. 19 that Spell had "a bit of plantar fasciitis," a condition that has different recovery times depending on the severity. So, whether Spell suits up on Friday against Baylor will be telling on his availability going forward. However, there was one offensive lineman ruled out for Friday: Tyler Gibson . It is set to be his third consecutive missed game. After making his 2026 debut on Saturday against BYU, Duane Thomas Jr. is now designated as probable for Friday's matchup against Baylor. The senior caught three passes for 16 yards and rushed twice for seven yards; a limited return to be sure. However, wide receivers coach Sean Beckton did say to 96.9 The Game on Oct. 21 that if coaches thought he could play more, he would. Plus, the Knights do not necessarily have to rush him back to a central role, given the target shares Josh Derry , Tyren Hornes and Waden Charles have accumulated. Meanwhile, after missing two games, sophomore Caleb Rollerson now has an opening to return to the field on Friday after being ruled questionable on Tuesday. Despite optimism from Frost on Monday about him being "really close," Lewis Carter has been ruled out for a fifth consecutive game. Jennings was also listed in Tuesday's report, designated as probable . However, it is still going to keep Swint out for at least one more week, which provides another opportunity for Landen Chambers to earn more carries out of the backfield, which he took advantage of against BYU. A trio of EDGEs was all designated probable: Sincere Edwards , Ken Talley and Bruno Dall . Baylor ruled out five of its players in its initial report. Defensive tackle Devonte Tezino started out the season as the Bears' starter, but an injury has kept him out of action since week three. Meanwhile, there are two Bears players designated as questionable : running back Dawson Pendergrass and cornerback Devon Jordan.

away.headline: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure
away.blurb: 5 Questionable Decisions That Defined Dave Aranda's Baylor Tenure Skip to main content SI.COM Here are five of the most questionable decisions of Aranda's Baylor tenure. Aranda had reason to overhaul Baylor's defensive staff following the 2022 season, but his choice of replacement proved questionable. Continuing to direct the defense while overseeing the entire program raised questions about whether Aranda had taken on too much. Although his defensive expertise was never in doubt, the arrangement potentially limited the attention he could devote to recruiting, roster construction and other head coaching duties. Dave Aranda's tenure at Baylor peaked in 2021, when the Bears won a program-record 12 games, captured the Big 12 championship and claimed a Sugar Bowl victory. Nearly five years later, he was fired following Saturday's 25-24 loss at Kansas, finishing his six-plus seasons in Waco with a 40-40 record. Baylor's decline can't be traced to a single mistake, but several of Aranda's decisions played a role in the program's inability to sustain its success. Some made sense at the time but ultimately backfired, while others were mistakes he later acknowledged. 1. Being Slow to Embrace the Transfer Portal Nov 22, 2025; Tucson, Arizona, USA; Detailed view of the jersey of Baylor Bears quarterback Sawyer Robertson (13) against the Arizona Wildcats at Casino Del Sol Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Aranda's emphasis on player development helped establish the culture behind Baylor's 2021 championship, but that same philosophy arguably kept the Bears from adapting quickly enough to college football's changing roster landscape. Baylor added only 10 scholarship transfers during Aranda's first three seasons before bringing in 12 during the 2023 cycle. While other programs increasingly used the portal to address immediate needs, the Bears remained more reliant on developing players already on their roster. Aranda later acknowledged struggling with bringing in transfers when doing so could mean passing over players he had recruited and developed. That reluctance became particularly costly following the 2021 season, when Baylor lost several important contributors, including Jalen Pitre, JT Woods, Terrel Bernard and Abram Smith. Replacing that experience and production was never going to be easy, but the transfer portal offered opportunities to address weaknesses before they became bigger problems. Instead, Baylor struggled to maintain the depth and physicality that had helped it win the conference championship. Aranda eventually became much more aggressive in the portal, but the adjustment came after Baylor had already fallen behind. 2. Failing to Balance NIL Investments Acros

home.headline: UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game
home.blurb: Coach Scott Frost said running back Taevion Swint will be back quickly, and linebacker Lewis Carter could be a game-time decision this week . He added that if the senior isn't available against the Baylor Bears, he'll likely be a game-time decision next Saturday against the Kansas Jayhawks . Carter has missed every conference game this season. He went into the medical tent for a knee injury at the end of Week 3's win over the Georgia State Panthers and was ruled out early for the next game. UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game UCFRoundtable 372 Members • 1,448 Posts UCFRoundtable UCFRoundtable Related stories (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) UCF's Scott Frost Shares Injury Updates Ahead of Space Game Demetrius Montero Partner Oct 27, 2026 9:00 PM Published Oct 27, 2026 9:00 PM Updated Oct 28, 2026 2:36 PM Fresh off an historic upset, the Knights could regain dynamic playmaker Taevion Swint and defensive leader Lewis Carter just in time for Friday’s high-stakes mission against Baylor. More Videos The UCF Knights made program history in upsetting the then-No. 2 BYU Cougars , and a few key players are on the cusp of returning for Friday's Space Game. Swint's injury occurred in practice, and Frost said he started limping after a "nothing play." The redshirt freshman missed his first game of the season , leaving room for Landen Chambers to step up in his absence. UCF has relied on the speedster to make plays in the run game and on special teams. Swint's rushed for 162 yards and two touchdowns on 32 carries, and returned seven kickoffs for 209 yards. He scored his first touchdown in the season opener against the Bethune-Cookman Wildcats, and the second in the Big 12 home opener against the TCU Horned Frogs . The Knights have missed their defensive quarterback, especially in highly contested losses against the then-No. 20 Houston Cougars and then-No. 18 Oklahoma State Cowboys . The senior had a career season last year after transferring from Oklahoma . Carter led the team with 92 tackles and set career highs in tackles for loss, sacks, and fumbles. He became a star at UCF. While at Oklahoma, he was a reserve linebacker and special teams player. Wisconsin transfer Tackett Curtis, the team's leading tackler, has stepped up in Carter's absence. Curtis has 42 tackles (18 solo, 24 assisted), one sack, one fumble recovery, one pass deflection and two interceptions. The Knights are getting healthy at the right time. They aim to build on an upset win and collect two more wins to break a two-year bowl drought. Friday's game against Baylor is one of the more interesting weekday matchups . The program fired coach David Aranda, and Joe Klanderman is the interim coach. UCF's eight-game Space Game winning streak ended in heartbreaking fashion as Houston caught the game-winning interception against former Knights quarterback Davi Belfort. Aranda's Bears handed the Knights one of their worst losses last season, 30-3. F

home.headline: BYU vs. UCF injury report: Two players listed for Cougars
home.blurb: Running back LJ Martin is listed as out, while starting offensive guard Kyle Sfarcioc is questionable. Running back Sione Moa and safety Tommy Prassas are both expected to be available for the game. One is running back LJ Martin , the 2025 Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year. ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that he'd miss 4-6 weeks after the TCU game, meaning he has roughly 2-4 weeks remaining on that diagnosis. That injury was expected, as Martin is listed as "Out." Starting offensive guard Kyle Sfarcioc is the other Cougar listed on the injury report, as he has a "Questionable" designation going into the game. BYU's offensive line has been one of the nation's best, with Sfarcioc a big part of it. He missed the game against Notre Dame, and the Cougars handled his absence very well in giving quarterback Bear Bachmeier ample time to throw. But getting back the 6-foot-4, 305-pound redshirt senior would provide another boost to this group, one they might need against a pesky UCF defense. On the other side, the Knights have six players listed as out, one listed as doubtful, three listed as questionable and six listed as probable. The BYU Cougars will soon take the field to match up against the UCF Knights in a Week 8 Big 12 matchup, with the game kicking off at 1:00 p.m. MT on Saturday. And in that game, the Cougars will be very healthy. In the latest injury report, the Cougars have just two players listed. Also of note is that running back Sione Moa is not on the injury report, as he suffered an injury against Utah Tech in the season-opener and was sidelined — up until this week, it seems. He was cleared to play against Notre Dame, but wasn't a go for confidence reasons, offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick told reporters. Safety Tommy Prassas, the team's third-leading tackler (23), is also a full-go after dealing with his own injury. Chris Vinel Daytona Beach News-Journal Oct. 25, 2026, 10:51 a.m. ET UCF head coach Scott Frost recalled past program triumphs during a recent upset win over No. 2 BYU. “UCF has come so far so fast,” he said before stopping. “And listen, back up. We can’t pat ourselves on the back over this win. We have to play a really good Baylor team in six days. So I’ve got to get all this out now. Frost stated the program's next goal is to become a perennial threat in the Big 12 conference. ORLANDO — Scott Frost admits it’s funny where his mind wanders. “I get in these zones,” he said. Even in the closing moments of the UCF Knights’ stunning 39-31 upset of No. 2 BYU on Oct. 24, a victory they hope signals something for their future, the head coach turned backward. Two familiar names popped into his brain. “I was sitting there on the fourth down and I go ‘Tre Neal.’ I just wanted somebody to get an interception like Tre Neal did,” Frost said. “And they kick off to us, I’m thinking ‘Mike Hughes.’” Hughes, of course, took a kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown to win the 2017 War on I-4 against South Florida and complete UCF’s undefeated regular season. In the American Athletic Conference title game a week later, Neal grabbed a championship-sealing interception in double overtime against Memphis. That was the last time the Knights went past regulation prior to Saturday’s BYU showdown. Point being, it’s not just fans that get sucked into those memories of bygone triumphs. Frost draws the parallels, too. This fall, Frost has shown his current players videos of iconic UCF moments. How it put itself on the FBS map by downing Alabama in 2000. How it legitimized the AAC with a Fiesta Bowl win over Baylor , despite being a 17-point underdog, on New Year’s Day 2014. How it staked its national championship claim by beating Auburn in the Peach Bowl exactly four years later. That marked the final game of Frost’s first term in charge in Orlando. He returned ahead of the 2025 campaign to the same program but a completely different landscape of college football. “At the beginning of the year, we talked about playing with a chip on our shoulder and earning some respect,” Frost said. The Knights have been there before — in many of the instances mentioned above. But here’s the bad part about nostalgia: It’s a trap. The past guarantees nothing for today’s outcome and certainly not tomorrow’s. Frost caught himself during his postgame press conference. “But UCF has come so far so fast, and we’ve cleared so many hurdles to get into the Big 12 and get where we are.” Then, the reflection ended, and Frost aimed forward. “The biggest hurdle we’ve got to clear is now being competitive and a winning program and then hopefully a perennial threat in the Big 12,” he said. “... Hopefully, this will boost us a little.”
